raw.description:
We’re building the next generation of employee benefits infrastructure.

At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.

Happl is backed by leading investors such as YCombinator, 6Degrees Capital, Haatch, Portage, and more, known for backing leading companies such as Deel, Rippling, Airbnb, Coinbase, Dropbox, and most recently was awarded a place in the UK’s top 100 startups for 2026.

About the role

As Financial Controller at Happl, you’ll own the financial engine of the business — everything from the cash in the bank to the numbers our board and investors use to make decisions runs through you. You’ll run the monthly close, the full revenue cycle, the compliance calendar across two jurisdictions, and our treasury position, and you’ll decide how all of it gets built, systemised, and automated.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role with a direct line to leadership. You won’t be managing a process someone else designed — you’ll be deciding what good looks like across revenue, cash, compliance, and reporting, then making it happen. You’ll work closely with the CEO, the board, our investors, and our outsourced bookkeeping, audit, and tax partners, holding all of it to a standard that matches the product we’ve built.

We’re FCA-regulated and YCombinator-backed, having raised $11m to date, and we give global employers a single place to design, deliver, and manage benefits across 160+ countries and 70+ languages — which means the finance function behind the product has to be just as sharp as the product itself. We’re entering our next phase of growth, with an ambitious revenue trajectory and an expanding international footprint, and this role sits at the centre of it.

What you’ll be doing

  • Owning the monthly close on a fixed timetable — management accounts, balance sheet integrity, accruals, prepayments, and the revenue and cost reconciliations that sit behind them

  • Writing the commentary that explains what’s actually happened in the business, not just what the numbers say

  • Producing the monthly investor reporting pack and the financial sections of board materials — ARR and revenue analysis, cash and runway, burn efficiency, unit economics, cohort and retention metrics, and budget versus actual

  • Owning the full revenue cycle — invoicing, collections, aged debt, and revenue recognition across a multi-currency, multi-contract subscription base

  • Leading the rollout of automated billing and revenue recognition tooling, moving us from manual tracking to a system that scales without adding headcount

  • Managing our two legal entities — a US TopCo and a UK operating company — including statutory accounts, audit preparation, intercompany accounting, transfer pricing mechanics, and FX exposure between them

  • Owning the compliance calendar end to end across both jurisdictions — UK VAT returns, corporation tax, US federal and state filings, sales tax where applicable, and payroll taxes

  • Supporting our FCA regulatory reporting obligations and the financial controls that sit behind them

  • Running monthly payroll across jurisdictions, pension and benefits administration, employee expenses, and the finance side of onboarding and offboarding

  • Owning the cash position and treasury strategy — cash flow forecasting, working capital, FX management, and structuring how we hold company funds to earn a sensible return without taking risk we shouldn’t

  • Managing our outsourced bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners — holding them to deadlines and quality, and pulling work in-house where doing so makes us faster

  • Owning the finance tech stack and having a strong opinion on it, actively replacing manual work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across reconciliations, invoice processing, variance analysis, and reporting drafts

  • Leveraging AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to speed up your own work and build the systems that let finance scale without adding headcount

  • Acting as the financial conscience of the business, with a direct line to the founders and a real say in how we grow

What we’re looking for

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA), or qualified by experience with a track record that stands up to scrutiny

  • Genuine ownership of a monthly close cycle and management reporting pack, start to finish

  • Strong technical grounding in revenue recognition, accruals accounting, and balance sheet control

  • Comfortable with tax and compliance across VAT, corporation tax, and payroll, ideally spanning both the UK and US

  • AI-native in your approach — you already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and can talk specifically about what you’ve automated and what it saved you

  • Exceptional attention to detail, alongside the judgement to know when precision matters and when speed does

  • A clear communicator — you can explain a number to a non-finance audience without patronising them or losing them

  • Ideally, SaaS or subscription business experience, particularly ARR reporting and deferred revenue, and familiarity with modern billing infrastructure like Xero or Stripe

  • Comfort with SQL, Python, or low-code automation tools is a bonus, not a requirement, but it will make your life here significantly easier

What to expect

Being Financial Controller at Happl is not a maintenance role. You’ll be building the finance function as you run it — choosing the systems, designing the controls, and deciding how billing, revenue recognition, and reporting should work as we scale into new markets and currencies. That’s not a caveat; it’s the role.

Some weeks will be genuinely rewarding — a reporting pack you built gives the board real clarity, a manual process you automated saves the team hours every month, a treasury decision you made puts real value on the table. Some will be hard — closing the books on a fixed timetable, holding partners and advisors to a deadline, and making judgement calls across two jurisdictions with incomplete information.

What you get in return is real scope. You’ll own the whole picture — revenue, cash, compliance, treasury, and reporting — across two jurisdictions and 160+ countries of operations, with a direct line to the founders and reporting that goes straight to the board and our investors. This is the foundation of a finance function that will grow with the business, and the right person grows with it.

Why join Happl

  • Be part of building something that genuinely matters — the future of how companies support their people

  • Competitive salary that reflects the impact you’ll have

  • Real equity — a meaningful stake in what we’re building together

  • Hybrid working from day one, with the trust and flexibility to do your best work

  • Your own Happl account — use the platform you’re helping to build and shape

  • Private Health Insurance, because we genuinely care about how you’re doing

  • Dental insurance, including family cover

  • A personal Wellbeing budget to spend however wellbeing works for you — no questions asked

  • A dedicated L&D budget to grow in the direction that excites you

  • Pension — we’re invested in your future, not just the short term

About the Interview

  • Stage 1: 20-min Intro call with Ben Shorrock (Head of Operations)

  • Stage 2: Short task

  • Stage 3: 30-min deep dive and task review with Ben T (CEO) & Ben S (Ops)

Additional Details

  • Location: London, Holborn

  • Team: Finance

  • Reports to: CEO

  • Working arrangement: Hybrid (4+ Days in Office)

raw.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We’re looking for a Broker Relationship Executive

As the face of iwoca to a wide range of UK brokers, you will act as a trusted advisor, problem solver, and relationship builder. From training brokers on our products to advocating for their deals internally and attending key industry events, you will be given the autonomy and support to take ownership of a high-impact portfolio and directly drive our market expansion.

The role

You will manage day-to-day interactions across our expanding UK network, with a strong focus on long-tail broker accounts. You will combine phone, email, LinkedIn, and face-to-face outreach to unlock partner potential, while leveraging internal data tools to track pipeline performance and maintain accurate CRM records.

Responsibilities

  • Proactively build iwoca’s presence across the UK by acquiring, engaging, and activating broker relationships across all communication channels.

  • Champion broker needs internally by collaborating with credit assessment, operations, and product teams to progress applications and resolve queries.

  • Deliver a seamless on-boarding experience for new brokers, guiding them step-by-step through their initial deal submissions.

  • Serve as the dedicated first point of contact for long-tail broker accounts outside of standard panels to support their ongoing daily requests.

  • Monitor activity metrics and pipeline data to spot engagement trends, identify high-potential partners, and step in to support at-risk relationships.

  • Conduct training sessions to keep partners up to date on iwoca policies, and represent the business at regional and industry networking events.

Requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve. To succeed as a Broker Relationship Executive, you’ll also bring:

  • A minimum of 2 years client management experience

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a professional phone manner, and confidence delivering presentations both in person and virtually via webinars.

  • Commercial curiosity with a genuine interest in financial products, third-party dynamics, and how brokers operate within the lending ecosystem.

  • Strong organisational skills and a self-directed approach, with a proven track record of managing a high-volume workload, prioritising your calendar, and taking ownership of new responsibilities to a high standard.

  • A confident, people-focused mindset, taking pride in personal contributions while thriving as a collaborative team player dedicated to building strong relationships.

  • Proficiency using CRM tools and dashboards to track broker engagement, monitor pipeline data, and manage a dispersed portfolio of accounts.

  • Willingness to travel via car or train for partner meetings and industry events, including occasional overnight stays.

The salary

We expect to pay from £35,000 - £50,000 + bonus for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

We’re looking for a Broker Relationship Manager

As a key driver of iwoca’s commercial growth, you will take ownership of a high-value broker portfolio across the UK. From running strategic performance reviews and delivering regional events to converting active pipelines and feeding market intelligence back to our product teams, you will be given the commercial autonomy to scale key partnerships and directly impact our bottom line.

The role

In this role, you will operate with independence to maximise panel performance, combining face-to-face partner engagement with data-driven pipeline tracking to ensure iwoca remains the lender of choice.

Responsibilities

  • Build and scale iwoca’s presence across the UK through proactive phone, face-to-face, LinkedIn, and email engagement to acquire and activate broker partners.

  • Drive conversions and maximise target contributions by managing application pipelines through every stage of the funnel and presenting competitive offers.

  • Deliver regional events, webinars, and training sessions to educate brokers on iwoca's systems, policies, and financial product structures.

  • Analyse broker and panel activity using performance dashboards to lead structured business reviews and identify commercial growth opportunities.

  • Collaborate with credit assessment, operations, and product teams to resolve complex broker queries and unblock stuck applications.

  • Gather competitor intelligence and market feedback during partner discussions to share actionable insights with the business and help shape our product offering.

Requirements

At iwoca we look for people who are smart, humble, motivated, and always striving to improve. To succeed as a Broker Relationship Manager, you’ll also bring:

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to lead face-to-face meetings, host webinars, and conduct structured performance reviews with external partners.

  • Solid understanding of financial product structures (including loan terms, pricing, and interest rates) to effectively handle complex broker queries and position our offering.

  • Strong commercial mindset with a track record of managing a high-volume portfolio, prioritising accounts based on commercial opportunity, and consistently striving to exceed targets.

  • High degree of self-organisation and accountability, with a proven ability to manage your diary, navigate new responsibilities autonomously, and deliver high-standard work.

  • A natural, people-focused approach that combines individual drive with collaborative teamwork and a passion for building lasting relationships.

  • Proficiency in using data tools and CRM dashboards to monitor pipeline activity, track engagement signals, and drive informed business conversations.

  • Flexibility to travel across the UK via car or train for regional meetings and events, including occasional overnight stays.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

The team sets its own goals and direction. It brings together engineers, data scientists, and product and strategy people. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. You'll lead two engineers and report to the head of engineering for iwoca's customer journey, from first application to repeat lending.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • Experimentation. You've built systems that run controlled experiments, especially long-running ones.

  • Legacy migration. You've moved business-critical logic out of a complex legacy monolith and kept everything that depends on it working.

  • Working with data scientists. You've worked with data scientists from prototype to production, and know their work well enough to challenge it.

raw.description:
About Juicebox

Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war.

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth, powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world.

Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.

About the Role

As an Enterprise Account Executive at Juicebox, you'll help drive our next stage of growth by partnering with mid-market and enterprise organizations to transform how they hire. You'll own complex sales cycles from discovery through close, working with senior Talent Acquisition, People, and Recruiting leaders to solve high-impact hiring challenges.

raw.title: Enterprise Account Executive
raw.description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

 

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

 

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

 

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

 

We have raised $14M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

The Role:

  • We are looking for Enterprise Account Executives.

  • This role is focused on selling into global enterprises with distributed teams, multiple buying centres, layered governance, and high data sensitivity. These are strategic accounts where the impact of accurate hierarchies and clean CRM data is measured in millions.

  • Our first ramped AEs are far exceeding quota, so we know the motion works.

  • Our early enterprise motion is working. We are generating strong demand and building pipeline within large organisations.

  • You will be responsible for driving high six-figure opportunities and are confident that we will close the first 7 figure deals this year through complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles.

  • Our targets call for millions of additional ARR over the next year. You will play a major role in that.

Important to Know:

  • Hours - This will be an exciting but intense job. Kernel is growing extremely fast and hours can often be long. Many of our customers are on the West Coast, and meetings can be held late in the evening.

  • Working location - Minimum 4 days a week in the London office (most people do 5). There will be international travel involved for this role in visiting prospects.

Responsibilities:

  • You’ll manage complex sales cycles with some of the best Enterprise businesses out there (5,000+ employees), from mid six-figure through to seven-figure+ deals.

  • Multi-thread within accounts and build executive-level relationships, including VP and C-level stakeholders.

  • Most opportunities will be sourced for you by the SDR team and Growth team, however sourcing additional pipeline is expected.

  • You’ll collaborate with the wider team on GTM strategy as we expand our ICP & experiment in other verticals.

  • You’ll help to create our sales processes as you build them.

  • You’ll become the best person in the company at explaining & pitching the product.

  • You’ll work closely with product, engineering, and customer success, bringing in insights from across the company and performing an essential part of our product feedback loop.

Your Traits:

  • Entrepreneurial: creative, resourceful.

  • Executive presence: You are comfortable engaging VPs, CROs, CIOs, and senior RevOps leaders.

  • All-in: hard-working, excited to stretch yourself, willing to take out the trash.

  • Clear thinker, good writer: you can crisply articulate your ideas, goals, and plans and help our customers make sense of hairy consulting-like problems.

Essential Qualifications:

  • 3-7 years of experience.

  • At least 1 year consistently closing deals worth $50k+/year in a multi-stakeholder sales process, consistently hitting six- to seven-figure targets.

  • Ability to execute on a consultative, solutions-oriented, value-based selling methodology (MEDDPICC).

  • Track record of consistent over-achievement in past sales roles.

  • Ability to discuss technical concepts with prospective customers and translate requirements into a demonstrable product.

  • Comfort negotiating and navigating contracts, security and legal discussions without support.

  • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal skills.

Nice-To-Have:

  • Startup/scale-up experience is a plus.

  • Experience selling to Revenue Operations, GTM and/or Sales teams.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

 

As Staff AI Deployment Strategist, you will shape how some of the most ambitious enterprises in the UK & Nordics region adopt frontier AI at scale.

This is a senior, high-impact role at the intersection of strategy, technology, and execution. You will work directly on Mistral’s most strategic opportunities and largest deliveries, helping customers move from ambition to measurable business outcomes. You will frame complex AI transformation programs, turn executive priorities into actionable roadmaps, and ensure that Mistral delivers systems that are valuable, scalable, and trusted.

You will also act as a senior sponsor on our most critical customer programs, bringing judgment, structure, and delivery excellence to high-stakes engagements. Your mandate is to raise the ambition and quality of AI adoption: helping customers identify where AI can create step-change value, making the right trade-offs, and ensuring that execution matches the strategic promise.

This role is ideal for an experienced strategy consultant, transformation leader, or senior operator who wants to move from advising on change to building it directly with frontier AI technology.

 

What You Will Do

  • Shape high-impact AI transformations

    • Partner closely with Mistral’s Sales leadership in the UK & Nordics to qualify opportunities, align on account strategy, and drive executive engagement.

    • Work with senior customer stakeholders to identify where frontier AI can create material business value.

    • Structure complex opportunities into clear, credible, and executable transformation programs.

    • Translate strategic ambition into delivery roadmaps, success metrics, and operating plans.

    • Help customers make the right trade-offs between ambition, feasibility, speed, and long-term scalability.

  • Sponsor Mistral’s most strategic deliveries

    • Act as a senior sponsor on the largest and most complex customer programs, primarily in the UK & Nordics and potentially cross-region as priorities evolve.

    • Ensure delivery quality, executive alignment, and measurable business impact.

    • Anticipate risks, unblock decisions, and help teams navigate ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

    • Bring senior judgment to moments where scope, resources, timelines, or expected value need to be clarified.

  • Build repeatable deployment excellence

    • Turn lessons from strategic engagements into reusable approaches, playbooks, and patterns.

    • Raise the bar for how AI programs are qualified, framed, delivered, and scaled.

    • Act as a senior relay for the Solutions organization in the region, helping teams adopt shared best practices, adapt them thoughtfully to local market specificities when needed, and strengthen the quality of execution.

    • Work hand in hand with Solutions leadership to connect customer realities, delivery patterns, and field feedback into practical ways of improving how Mistral deploys AI.

    • Help codify what great enterprise AI deployment looks like across industries and use cases.

    • Contribute to a Solutions culture that combines strategic clarity, technical depth, and strong execution.

  • Develop and multiply senior DS impact

    • Coach Deployment Strategists on strategic problem-solving, executive communication, and delivery leadership.

    • Help teams raise the quality of their work on the highest-impact opportunities.

    • Identify capability gaps and contribute to hiring, staffing, and development priorities.

    • Act as a force multiplier across accounts, teams, and regions where your experience can have the highest leverage.

 
 

What We're Looking For

 

You are a senior, highly capable professional with strong executive presence, excellent business judgment, and a track record of leading complex strategic or transformation work.

Typical indicators we’re looking for include:

  • 8–10+ years of professional experience in strategy consulting, digital transformation, AI, enterprise technology, or a similarly demanding environment.

  • Experience operating at Partner, Principal, Engagement Manager, Director, or equivalent level in a top-tier strategy consulting or transformation context.

  • A strong ability to structure ambiguous problems, identify value, and turn strategy into execution.

  • Experience leading large accounts, complex programs, or senior customer relationships.

  • The credibility to engage with executives and C-level stakeholders on business priorities, trade-offs, and impact.

  • Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to challenge assumptions constructively.

  • Comfort working at the frontier of technology, even when solutions are evolving quickly and the path is not fully defined.

  • A low-ego, high-ownership mindset and a desire to build with customers and teams, not just advise from a distance.

  • Fluency in English; German is a strong plus.

 

Hiring Process

 

• Talent Acquisition screening call

• 30min Hiring Manager Interview

• 45min Business Acumen Interview 

• 60min Technical Deep Dive on LLMs

• Panel (Home Prep & Restitution)

• 30min Value Talk

• Reference check

 

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

We are looking for a hands-on Medical Recruiter to help us scale our UK clinical teams. This is a delivery-focused role: you will own the full recruitment lifecycle, from intake and sourcing through interviews, offer and close, across a range of clinical and medical roles.

Our clinical teams are at the heart of the Neko experience. They deliver the care that helps our members start their preventative health journey, so every hire directly shapes the quality of that care. We are moving quickly, and this hiring is about precision and pace. You will work closely with hiring managers and clinical leaders to hire outstanding professionals who want to work in a tech-enabled, forward-thinking environment.

What you'll do in the first 6-12 Months

  • End-to-end recruitment for UK clinical and medical roles (e.g. doctors, advanced nurse practitioners, registered nurses, healthcare assistants, biomedical scientists, echocardiographers, clinical operations), managing a full requisition load against agreed hiring plans.

  • Source proactively across job boards, direct outreach, referrals, professional networks and events, and adjust channels based on response and conversion data.

  • Own the candidate experience from first contact to offer, with clear communication and fast turnaround at every stage.

  • Keep Ashby accurate and current, so pipeline reporting and Workday alignment can be trusted without manual cleanup.

  • Use data to track pipeline performance, identify bottlenecks, and continuously improve hiring outcomes.

Minimum Requirements

  • 3 to 5 years of recruitment experience, ideally hiring healthcare professionals in the UK or in other regulated, high-volume environments such as luxury retail, hospitality or similar service-led settings where standards and pace both matter.

  • Proven success hiring talent from top-performing companies, scale-ups, or mission-driven organisations.

  • Strong sourcing capabilities with a creative, research-led approach to finding exceptional talent.

  • Self-sufficient, proactive and comfortable operating in fast-moving, high-context environments.

  • Clear, professional communication with clinicians and internal teams alike.

  • Comfortable using AI tools to speed up sourcing, outreach and admin, and to sharpen your own judgment.

  • Familiarity with UK clinical registration and pre-employment checks (GMC, NMC, HCPC, DBS, right to work) is helpful, but not essential. We’ll teach you the rest.

We offer a dynamic work environment with a high degree of autonomy that fosters growth and development. If you are passionate about building a better healthcare system for everyone and you thrive in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you.

raw.description:

Role Purpose

The Member Experience Training & Quality Specialist makes the Neko member experience standard real on the ground. You deliver our member experience training to teams across the business, primarily clinic teams and centralised support teams, and you run the quality assurance activity that tells us whether the standard is actually landing in practice.

This is a delivery role at the heart of a live culture change programme. You will facilitate training that shifts mindset, not just process, run experience audits against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, and turn what you see into coaching and improvement. As markets scale, you keep the standard consistent across every site and cohort, and rising over time.

You own the coordination and logistics that keep training and quality assurance running: scheduling sessions and audits, and organising the people, spaces and materials each one needs. You report to the Hospitality Programme Lead and support the wider rollout, so you will also play a hands-on part in projects and launch activity as new clinics and teams come online.

What You’ll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Stage 1 and Stage 2 member experience training delivered consistently to every new clinic cohort in your market, with 30-day reviews showing the mindset shift is landing, not just attendance being logged. (Member First, always)

  • A regular quality assurance rhythm is live: experience audits across clinic and support teams, scored consistently against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, with clear findings shared back to the teams and their leads. (Impact, not activity)

  • Audit insight turned into action: recurring friction points named early and at least two concrete experience improvements implemented with clinic and support leads. (Optimistic truth-seeking)

  • Support team training built out and delivered alongside clinic training, so centralised member support holds the same standard as the clinic floor. (Chase 10X, not 10%)

  • The ongoing learning ecosystem running smoothly, including the monthly AI role play and quiz, with completion tracked and shared with Clinic Leads as a coaching tool, not a performance measure. (Tech-enabled, human-centred)

  • A training and audit calendar owned end to end: sessions scheduled around clinic rotas and cohort timing, facilitators, rooms, materials and joining details arranged, and audits planned on a set cadence so every site and team is covered without gaps. (Impact, not activity)

Minimum Requirements

  • 3+ years in training delivery, learning and development, hospitality, or member and customer experience, ideally in a high-touch service, hospitality, or premium retail environment.

  • A confident facilitator, comfortable leading a room of clinicians and operators and holding attention and energy across a full-day session.

  • Hands-on experience running quality assurance or experience audits, mystery shopping, or service standard reviews, with the ability to score consistently and give feedback that changes behaviour.

  • A sharp eye for service detail and what separates a good experience from an exceptional one, drawn from service design and hospitality thinking rather than process alone.

  • Organised and self-directed, able to run a training and audit calendar across multiple sites and cohorts without dropping the standard.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the credibility to influence teams and leads who do not report to you.

  • Willingness to travel regularly between clinic sites, and occasionally between markets.

  • Experience supporting a multi-site clinic, hospitality, or retail rollout as it scales.

  • Experience with digital learning tools, an LMS, or AI-enabled training and assessment.

  • Confident with everyday workplace tools, including Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook, to build training materials, track audits and report findings.

Hiring Process

Candidates progress from application and structured screening through thoughtfully designed interviews culminating in a formal offer and final pre-employment checks before joining the team.

Neko Health is committed to inclusive hiring and member-first care. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to request reasonable adjustments to support your application.

Introducing Neudata:

Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.

With offices in London, New York, and Shanghai and a team of 100 people, we connect a vast global network of buyers and providers through our market-leading platforms and specialist consulting - and by providing a clear view of the data landscape, we help organisations navigate complexity and find their competitive edge. We're looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial Sales Director to take our Scout and Ranger platforms to data buyers across EMEA and APAC: hedge funds, asset managers, private equity firms and the fast-growing world of AI. This is a pure new business role, and you'll own your territory end to end, from spotting the opportunity through to signing the deal.

raw.title: 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist/Engineer
raw.description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You’ll join our Research Team in London as a 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist/Engineer — working at both ends of the pipeline, from cutting-edge academic research to shipping directly to customers. Our team builds the reconstruction technology that turns casually captured or domain-specific imagery into high-fidelity 3D reconstructions: everything from Structure-from-Motion through 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward models, and generative models. We’ve shipped 360 splatting to consumers and enterprise customers, developed the splatting tech that runs on phones, and published at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and SIGGRAPH — more often than not, our papers end up in production.

You’ll work alongside world-class researchers in computer vision, machine learning, graphics, and robotics on large-scale spatial understanding, localization, reconstruction, scene understanding, and geospatial foundation models. This role is open to junior and senior researchers; scope and responsibility are calibrated to your experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Research & Publication — Conduct original research in 3D computer vision, machine learning, and spatial AI; publish findings at top-tier venues including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and SIGGRAPH.

  • Algorithm Development — Design, implement, and evaluate novel algorithms across 3D reconstruction, neural scene representations, 3D Gaussian Splatting, SfM, meshing, geometric deep learning, feed-forward models, generative models, and spatial foundation models.

  • Research-to-Production — Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to transition promising ideas into customer-facing products — working directly with real capture conditions, real hardware constraints, and real customers on short turnarounds.

  • Large-Scale Experimentation — Build and run large-scale experiments and benchmarking frameworks to rigorously validate and advance new methods.

  • Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration — Partner with world-class researchers in CV, ML, graphics, and robotics to advance large-scale spatial understanding, localization, reconstruction, and geospatial foundation models.

  • Rapid Prototyping — Implement and iterate on state-of-the-art methods for both academic publishing and production deployment, delivering working prototypes to enterprise customers with speed and quality.

What You’ll Bring

  • PhD in Computer Vision, Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a closely related field — or equivalent demonstrated research experience in industry.

  • A strong research track record in 3D computer vision: reconstruction, depth estimation, novel view synthesis, SfM, SLAM, or closely related areas.

  • A meaningful publication record at top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or equivalent).

  • Strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch.

  • Evidence that you can carry an idea from research into something real — a shipped feature, a production pipeline, a widely used open-source release, or similar.

  • The independence to drive research projects from idea generation through experimentation, publication, and handoff.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with classical reconstruction tooling (COLMAP or similar).

  • C++ or CUDA experience, and a feel for performance and on-device constraints.

  • Experience with traditional 3D techniques — meshing, texturing, or bringing modern geometry or generative representations into native 3D.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Location & Work Model

This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office.

Inclusive Application

We know the strongest candidates don’t always tick every box. If you’re excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we’re looking for.

Equal Opportunity

Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.

Candidate Privacy

I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial’s Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice.

raw.title: AI Deployment Lead
raw.description:
Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

As an AI Deployment Lead / Applied AI Consultant, you'll work directly with our most strategic customers to understand their objectives and key challenges, identify high-impact AI opportunities, and translate them into measurable business value.

You'll be building AI solutions on Omnea's procurement automation platform, combining the structured data flowing through requests, approvals, contracts, and supplier records with AI. Omnea gives AI the operational context of how a business actually buys, so it can move past answering questions and start taking action inside procurement itself: routing requests, flagging risk, drafting contract terms, negotiating with suppliers. There is no AI without that context.

You'll prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realisation, growing Omnea's footprint at those customers as you go.

This customer-facing role is ideal for people who enjoy working directly with customers and turning complex business challenges into practical AI solutions. The focus is on problem framing, solution design, and business impact rather than pure implementation. While you will prototype AI solutions, the primary goal is to deliver meaningful business value to customers.

What You'll Do

  • Identify High-Impact AI Opportunities: Work closely with enterprise customers to understand their strategic priorities and operational challenges, identifying where AI can deliver measurable business value.

  • Design AI-Powered Solutions: Translate complex business problems into scalable solution architectures, using Omnea's AI to eliminate manual work across procurement.

  • Prototype and Demonstrate Value: Rapidly build prototypes and proof-of-value solutions that demonstrate tangible outcomes to business and technical stakeholders.

  • Lead AI Innovation with Customers: Facilitate workshops, hackathons, and innovation sessions with customers to explore new ways AI can transform their operations.

  • Drive Adoption and Business Impact: Partner with customer teams to ensure successful implementation, adoption, and realisation of measurable value from AI deployments.

  • Develop Domain Expertise: Build deep expertise in specific industries or business domains (e.g., supply chain, finance) and help scale that knowledge across the organisation.

What's Different About This Role

  • You'll spend more time on problem framing and validation than on hand-building every proof of value. AI can generate a working prototype fast; your job is deciding whether it actually solves the customer's problem.

  • Writing a sharp brief for what you want AI to build is now core to the role, not a side skill.

  • Judgment on business impact matters more than raw build speed: which use case actually moves the metric the customer cares about, and which is just an impressive demo.

  • You'll keep pushing on what's possible as Omnea's AI tooling evolves, and bring what you learn back to the rest of the team.

About You

You might be a great fit if you…

  • have 5+ years of experience in solutions consulting, data / AI consulting, technical pre-sales, sales engineering, value engineering, or customer-facing solution-architecture or AI roles

  • enjoy translating business challenges into technical solutions

  • can communicate complex technical concepts to business and executive stakeholders

  • have a good understanding of business processes across procurement, finance, and supply chain, with the ability to translate high-level business needs into specific AI use cases

  • demonstrate strong presentation skills to both internal and external stakeholders (including executives), whether whiteboarding sessions or formal readouts and demos

Procurement is a harder interface problem than it sounds. Approval workflows that branch and re-route, dense tables people live in all day, intake forms that adapt to what someone is buying.   • Join a Skilled Team. Become part of one of Europe's fastest-growing software companies, working alongside experienced full-stack product engineers and product designers from top technology businesses and startups.

  • AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude Code and agentic workflows every day to write, review, and ship code faster, and our product is itself built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows.

  • Continuous Delivery. We deploy small, incremental changes to production multiple times per day, enabling rapid iteration and fast customer feedback loops.

  • Collaboration and Autonomy. We operate as a high-trust team where individuals are expected to take ownership while collaborating closely to solve difficult problems.

  • Customers at the Center. We regularly engage directly with customers to understand their problems, gather feedback, and ensure we're building products that create genuine value.

  • You're deep in React. You've built complex, production React applications and you understand the framework properly, not just the API surface. Rendering behaviour, state, performance, and where things break at scale.

  • You've owned front-end infrastructure. Rendering strategies, build tooling, bundle performance, and the architectural decisions underneath a large application.

  • You've built or owned a design system. Not just consumed one. You've made the calls on component APIs, driven adoption across teams, and dealt with the messy reality of migration and versioning.

  • You have taste. You care how things look and feel, you notice when something is only 90% right, and you can hold a genuine conversation with designers rather than just implementing tickets.

  • You're a strong engineer first. Your depth and your interest sit in the front end, and that's the point of this role. But you're fluent in TypeScript generally and comfortable working beyond the browser when a problem calls for it.

  • You're motivated by impact. You care about what your work actually achieves, not just how it's built. You thrive with the autonomy to make meaningful decisions and take real ownership of outcomes.

raw.title: Full-Stack Software Engineer, Child Safety Tools & Systems (London)
raw.description:
About the Team

The Intelligence & Investigations Engineering team builds systems that detect, analyze, and disrupt abuse across OpenAI’s products. We partner closely with the Child Safety team and cross-functional groups to protect users while advancing OpenAI’s goal of developing AI that benefits everyone.

About the Role

As a Fullstack Engineer focused on child safety, you’ll build data-intensive, AI-powered applications and infrastructure that enable operators and investigators to work effectively and responsibly. You’ll adapt quickly in ambiguous, fast-moving environments to deliver well-crafted, reliable tooling for high-severity safety work.

*Candidates should understand this role involves exposure to sensitive and egregious content.


In this role, you will:

  • 7+ years of experience as a software engineer

  • Prototype, build, and maintain intelligence systems that detect, triage, and enable efficient human review of possible high severity harm

  • Work hand in hand with operators and investigators, designing and delivering systems that enable them to do their work faster, more accurately, and more safely.

  • Develop across the stack: UIs, services, pipelines, and anything else required to solve the problems we face.

  • Interact with partners across Product Policy, Platform Integrity, Safety Systems, and Research

  • Contribute to the team’s technical strategy, especially for child safety related tools and systems

  • Report on impact in a data-driven fashion

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong software engineering foundation and enjoy owning systems end-to-end—from infrastructure and data ingestion to frontend tooling

  • Are energized by working at the frontier of AI capabilities, integrating new models and APIs into practical systems

  • Have experience building and operating large-scale data pipelines or search/retrieval systems

  • Are proficient in Python and/or TypeScript, and familiar with tools like Spark, Kafka, Flink, data warehouses, and SQL

  • Take a product-minded approach, design with user workflows in mind, and iterate quickly based on feedback

  • Favor pragmatic solutions and can ship in hacky, low-support environments when needed

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and open-ended problem spaces with evolving goals

  • Have prior experience working on engineering for high-severity harms

  • Bring intuition for the pain points and workflows of operations and investigative teams, and curiosity about solving complex investigations

  • Bonus: prior knowledge of child-safety-specific challenges such as secure handling of quarantined content and reporting to NCMEC

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

raw.title: Head of Operations
raw.description:
🌍 About Outpost

Global expansion is broken. Without a local entity, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it or expand slowly and expensively.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need — tax, payments, treasury, or operations — and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we act as Merchant of Record, taking on tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We operate across 58+ tax jurisdictions for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack — payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for our Head of Operations: the person who owns how Outpost actually runs.

Today, operations at Outpost is a set of processes held together by a small group of very good people. Merchant onboarding, KYC/KYB, market launches, tax registrations, payouts, treasury approvals, chargebacks, merchant support — it all works, but it works because people push it. Your job is to turn that into a machine.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a management layer. You'll own the operational stack end to end: onboarding and activation, merchant operations, payments and treasury ops, compliance monitoring, and new market launches. You'll design the processes, build the tooling requirements with engineering, write the playbooks, and then run them yourself until they're good enough to hand over.

You'll hire and grow a small team behind you, but for the first stretch you are the team. If your instinct when something breaks is to open the dashboard and fix it rather than schedule a meeting about it, you'll do well here.

You'll work directly with the CEO and founding team, and you'll have a real say in what Outpost builds — operations is the sharpest source of product signal we have.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return, you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10–20 years to access.

You'll own a core function of a company solving one of the hardest problems in global commerce, work with senior stakeholders across PSPs, banks, tax authorities and merchants, and build a team from scratch. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Own the operational stack

  • Own merchant onboarding end to end: applications, KYC/KYB, risk review, activation, time-to-live

  • Run merchant operations day to day — support escalations, payouts, settlements, disputes

  • Own treasury operations: proceeds requests, money movement, reserves, reconciliation

  • Monitor merchant risk and compliance thresholds (chargebacks, fraud, refunds) and act before they become losses

  • Own payment operations alongside engineering: auth rates, routing, decline recovery, chargeback and fraud strategy

Build the system, not just the output

  • Turn manual processes into documented, repeatable, measurable playbooks

  • Define the operational metrics that matter and build the reporting so the company can see them

  • Work with engineering to spec and prioritise internal tooling — you are the customer for our internal ops platform

  • Kill work: automate, template, or delete anything that doesn't need a human

  • Make Outpost able to double merchant volume without doubling ops headcount

Launch and scale

  • Launch new markets with full legal, tax, payments, and operational setup

  • Onboard new PSPs, banking partners, and local acquiring in new geographies

  • Build the operational side of new products and merchant segments before they go live

  • Feed market and merchant reality back into the product roadmap

Lead

  • Hire, onboard, and grow a small operations team

  • Set standards: what good looks like, how fast we respond, what we never get wrong

  • Be the operational voice in company planning — what we can support, when, and at what cost

💥 Example Projects

  • Redesign merchant onboarding to cut time-to-live by 50% without weakening KYB

  • Build the operational launch playbook for three new markets and run the first one yourself

  • Debug delays in payouts and fix them across engineering, ops, compliance, and PSPs

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Build the ops metrics dashboard: onboarding funnel, time-to-live, ticket volume, payout SLA, chargeback rate

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Spec the next version of our internal ops tooling with engineering and ship it

  • Write the merchant VAT compliance playbook across EU markets with the tax team

  • Hire and onboard the first two operations analysts and get them productive in 30 days

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • 6–10 years in operations at high-growth fintech, payments, or e-commerce infrastructure (Revolut, Stripe, Adyen, Wise, Mollie, Airwallex, Checkout.com, or similar)

  • Has owned a function or a large slice of one — onboarding, merchant ops, payment ops, or risk ops — not just executed within it

  • Experience building processes from zero, not inheriting them

  • Bonus: MoR platforms (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), cross-border tax exposure, or PSP/acquirer operations

  • Comfortable with data — SQL, spreadsheets, dashboards. You measure before you decide

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action — you solve, not observe

  • Systems thinker who still does the work — you fix the ticket and then remove the reason it existed

  • Analytically strong — you can quantify a process, not just describe it

  • Strong EQ — you know how to read a room, a customer, or a blocker

  • Exceptionally hard working — you see work as a core part of your purpose

  • Fluent in ambiguity and chaos — startups are not neat, this will be hard

  • Curious and resourceful — you can figure anything out

  • Comfortable getting hands dirty — your default mode is to do, not delegate

  • Clear, quantified achievements on your CV (not vague descriptions)

What this role is not:

  • Not a people-management role where you run a team that does the work

  • Not a process-maintenance role — nothing here is finished

  • Not a single-function specialist who wants to stay in payments, or compliance, or support

  • Not someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

This isn't about maintaining processes — it's about building the operating system of Outpost from the ground up. You won't just be in the room, you'll be writing the agenda.

Operations at an MoR is not a back-office function. It is the product. How fast merchants go live, whether money arrives on time, whether we catch risk before it costs us — that's what customers buy and where our margin lives. You'll own it.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

🦾 Outpost Team

Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen and Wayflyer — and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs.

🧾 What We Offer

  • Equity and salary in a well-funded startup

  • Ability to own your work and move fast

  • World-class training from operators who've scaled globally

  • A global mission with real impact

  • Low politics, high output

  • Chance to grow into a senior leadership role

  • A culture of builders, not talkers

🧭 Working Style

We work together in person in London 5 days a week. We believe the hardest problems are solved in the room.

🌎 Reach Out

Learn more

  1. Outpost Culture

  2. Outpost founder

Outpost is where the hard problems are. If you want to help build the engine behind global trade, we'd love to hear from you.

raw.description:
Payment Operations Lead

Global expansion is broken. Without a local company, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it, or expand slowly and expensively.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for a Payment Operations hire to own the part of Outpost where the money actually moves.

When we become the legal reseller in a market, we take the payment. Every merchant we onboard gets its own merchant ID and its own merchant category code, never pooled into one shared code, which is exactly why our approval rates beat the alternatives. Keeping that true across every market, every processor and every merchant is the job.

This is a quantitative role in an operational seat. You'll live in the transaction data: why authorisation rates differ by market, issuer, card type and hour of day, what a routing change is actually worth, where a 40 basis point cost difference is hiding, which decline codes are recoverable and which are noise. Then you'll act on it, with processors, with engineering, and with merchants.

You won't be siloed. Payments at Outpost touches pricing, treasury, tax and the product roadmap, and you'll be pulled into all of it. But your edge is the numbers, and we want someone whose first instinct on any problem is to pull the data and model it.

You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

You'll own economics that decide whether the company is profitable, negotiate with processors and banks as a principal rather than a customer, and get to see the full machinery of cross-border payments from the inside. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Build the system

  • Run payment operations agentically. Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. You'll design the workflows, set the guardrails, and audit what the agents produce

  • Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling

  • Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets

Own payments performance

  • Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves

  • Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate

  • Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling

  • Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits

  • Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it

Own the economics

  • Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks

  • Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation

  • Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call

  • Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants

Own the money movement

  • Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down

  • Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile

  • Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies

💥 Example Projects

  • Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it

  • Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market

  • Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data

  • Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching

  • Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia

  • Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar.

  • 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar)

  • Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team.

  • Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action. You solve, you don't observe

  • Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it

  • Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke

  • Strong EQ. Processors, banks and merchants all need managing, often at the same time

  • Exceptionally hard working. You see work as a core part of your purpose

  • Fluent in ambiguity and chaos. Startups are not neat, this will be hard

  • Curious and resourceful. You can figure anything out

  • Clear, quantified achievements on your CV, not vague descriptions

What this role is not:

  • Not a payments strategy role without operational depth. You'll be in the dashboards daily

  • Not a pure analytics role. The analysis is the start, the change is the job

  • Not a narrow specialist seat. Payments here touches pricing, treasury, tax and product

  • Not for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

Most companies treat payments as a cost centre someone else manages. Here it is the product and the margin at the same time.

We take legal responsibility for our merchants' payments. That means a point of approval rate is real revenue for them and real evidence for us, and a basis point of cost is real profit. Very few people get to own that surface this early, with this much data and this little bureaucracy in the way.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

We work together in person in London 5 days a week. We believe the hardest problems are solved in the room.

raw.title: Revenue Operations Lead
raw.description:
Revenue Operations Lead

Global expansion is broken. Without a local company, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it, or expand slowly and expensively.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for our first Revenue Operations hire: the person who owns how revenue actually works at Outpost.

Your job is to build the RevOps machine. One source of truth for pipeline. One model that turns a merchant's volume, markets and product mix into a price. One set of numbers that the CEO, the board and the commercial team all agree on. And a handover from signed contract to live merchant that never drops anything.

This is a hands-on build role, not a reporting layer. You'll sit between sales, marketing, and operations, and you'll be the only person who can see the whole revenue system at once. You'll design it, instrument it, automate it, and then run it until it's good enough to hand over.

You'll work directly with the CEO, the Chief of Staff and the founding team.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

You'll own a core function at a company solving one of the hardest problems in global commerce, you'll see every commercial decision before it happens, and you'll build a function from scratch with real budget and real backing. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Own the revenue system

  • Own the CRM (Attio) end to end: object model, stage definitions, required fields, hygiene, automation

  • Build the forecasting system and operationalise it with weekly pipeline review, monthly board numbers, and quarterly planning

  • Own the GTM stack: outbound sequencing, enrichment, routing, deduplication, attribution

  • Run the pipeline agentically. Build agentic system that enrich accounts, draft follow-ups, surface stalled deals and keep the CRM clean, so the team spends its time on the conversations and not the admin.   • Set the standard for what good data looks like, and hold the line on it

  • Hire behind you once the system is running

🧱 What We're Looking For
