Ironclad is scaling rapidly across EMEA through a partner-first go-to-market model. We’re looking for an entrepreneurial, proactive EMEA Partner Success Manager to shape and operationalise our Global Partner Services programs—building effective partner engagement, enablement, readiness, and collaboration across the region.

As part of Customer Value, you’ll support partner services across the customer lifecycle, from pre-sales alignment and delivery readiness through co-delivery and post-live adoption. Working with major systems integrators and consulting firms, you’ll help evolve a value-focused model that starts earlier in the customer journey and extends beyond implementation to improve conversion, accelerate time to value, increase platform usage, and strengthen long-term customer outcomes.

You’ll bring a strong operator’s mindset: turning ambiguity into clear, repeatable ways of working across Sales, Alliances, Technical Services, Customer Success, and external partners. You’ll use data to improve program performance and, based in London, spend regular time in the office and face-to-face with partners to build relationships and help them succeed.

What you'll do:

  • Own relationships with strategic partners’ practice and delivery leaders, aligning on priorities, readiness, quality expectations, capacity, and growth opportunities.

  • Partner with Sales, Alliances, and Customer Value to match qualified opportunities with the right partner, co-delivery model, and implementation approach based on customer needs, deal context, partner readiness, and expectations.

  • Operationalise partner engagement across the customer lifecycle—from discovery and scoping through readiness planning, delivery transition, and post-live support—clarifying roles and setting engagements up for execution and adoption.

  • Evolve partner programs with Partner Alliances, Enablement, and Customer Value leadership, including co-delivery and subcontracting frameworks, onboarding, certification, methodology alignment, delivery quality, and ongoing enablement.

  • Assess partner capacity, coverage, skills, and readiness against business demand and EMEA growth priorities; coordinate capacity planning across strategic and subcontracting relationships to improve predictability.

  • Build targeted partner enablement plans across product knowledge, implementation, integrations, value selling, customer change management, AI use cases, and emerging AI consumption models; help partners adapt capabilities and commercial/delivery approaches as opportunities evolve.

  • Work with EA and partner teams to understand partner ISV offerings, technology ecosystems, integrations, and customer architecture requirements, and connect differentiated capabilities to customer opportunities.

  • Help partner-led engagements establish a path to customer enablement, adoption, value realisation, and sustained platform usage after go-live; reinforce accountability for agreed post-live milestones.

  • Identify patterns in partner-led work that affect conversion, delivery quality, time to value, adoption health, renewal readiness, and expansion potential; translate findings into practical program improvements.

  • Establish an EMEA partner operating rhythm (in partnership with EMEA Partner Alliances) —including business reviews, readiness and capacity assessments, enablement planning, and escalation management—and keep partners current on regional priorities, market dynamics, customer needs, and product and go-to-market changes.

  • Maintain operational hygiene and data integrity for partner-led projects and programs across internal systems, reporting, and workflows; translate feedback from European partners and customers into actionable recommendations for Ironclad teams.

What success looks like:

  • A scalable EMEA partner-first operating model and a clear, consistent operating rhythm.

  • Better alignment between partner strategy and qualified deal motions, with greater confidence in partner fit, readiness, and implementation approach before kickoff.

  • More predictable partner capacity and targeted capability plans, with priority enablement gaps owned and closed.

  • Consistent, high-quality partner-led and co-delivered services, with clear roles across EA, Sales, Alliances, Services, Customer Value, and partners.

  • Partners equipped to respond to EMEA priorities and AI-led opportunities; partner ISV and integration capabilities connected to relevant customer needs.

  • Improved customer time to value, adoption, sustained usage, and expansion outcomes, with a positive contribution to adoption health, GRR, and NDR-oriented outcomes.

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years of experience in Professional Services, Partner Operations, Customer Success, Implementation, or a related role at a SaaS company and/or consulting or systems integration firm.

  • 2+ years of experience working with implementation partners, subcontractors, or partner delivery teams in a services environment.

  • Experience supporting complex pre-sales, scoping, or solution-alignment motions with Sales, Services, and/or Alliances teams; implementation, managed, partner services, or GSI experience is highly relevant.

  • Strong program management skills and a track record of building or improving cross-functional processes spanning internal teams and external partners.

  • Ability to bring structure to ambiguity and execute repeatable operating models in a fast-changing environment.

  • Strong relationship-building, influencing, and communication skills, including the ability to work with senior stakeholders across functions and geographies and turn complex considerations into clear recommendations.

  • Comfort using data and KPIs to evaluate program effectiveness and improve conversion, delivery quality, adoption, and customer outcomes.

  • Experience with change management, adoption planning, or value realisation is strongly preferred; understanding how to set partners up across sales, delivery, enablement, integrations, and customer outcomes is important.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset, sound judgment, and comfort shaping a partner-first model as the business scales and the operating model evolves.

  • Willingness to spend regular time in the London office and travel across Europe (approximately 15%).

  • Fluency in an additional European language, particularly German or French, is beneficial but not required.

UK Full-Time Employee Benefits at Ironclad:

  • Private Medical & Dental insurance, covered at 100% for you and dependents

  • Life assurance and Income Protection

  • Generous leave policies, including parental leave, medical leave and compassionate leave

  • Family-forming support through Maven for you and your partner

  • Monthly stipends for wellbeing, hybrid work, and (if applicable) phone use

  • Standard pension contribution scheme

  • Regular team events to connect, recharge, and have fun

  • And most importantly: the opportunity to help build the company you want to work at

Working with major systems integrators and consulting firms, you’ll help evolve a value-focused model that starts earlier in the customer journey and extends beyond implementation to improve conversion, accelerate time to value, increase platform usage, and strengthen long-term customer outcomes.

You’ll bring a strong operator’s mindset: turning ambiguity into clear, repeatable ways of working across Sales, Alliances, Technical Services, Customer Success, and external partners. You’ll use data to improve program performance and, based in London, spend regular time in the office and face-to-face with partners to build relationships and help them succeed.

What you'll do:

  • Own relationships with strategic partners’ practice and delivery leaders, aligning on priorities, readiness, quality expectations, capacity, and growth opportunities.

  • Partner with Sales, Alliances, and Customer Value to match qualified opportunities with the right partner, co-delivery model, and implementation approach based on customer needs, deal context, partner readiness, and expectations.

  • Operationalise partner engagement across the customer lifecycle—from discovery and scoping through readiness planning, delivery transition, and post-live support—clarifying roles and setting engagements up for execution and adoption.

  • Evolve partner programs with Partner Alliances, Enablement, and Customer Value leadership, including co-delivery and subcontracting frameworks, onboarding, certification, methodology alignment, delivery quality, and ongoing enablement.

  • Assess partner capacity, coverage, skills, and readiness against business demand and EMEA growth priorities; coordinate capacity planning across strategic and subcontracting relationships to improve predictability.

  • Build targeted partner enablement plans across product knowledge, implementation, integrations, value selling, customer change management, AI use cases, and emerging AI consumption models; help partners adapt capabilities and commercial/delivery approaches as opportunities evolve.

  • Work with EA and partner teams to understand partner ISV offerings, technology ecosystems, integrations, and customer architecture requirements, and connect differentiated capabilities to customer opportunities.

  • Help partner-led engagements establish a path to customer enablement, adoption, value realisation, and sustained platform usage after go-live; reinforce accountability for agreed post-live milestones.

  • Identify patterns in partner-led work that affect conversion, delivery quality, time to value, adoption health, renewal readiness, and expansion potential; translate findings into practical program improvements.

  • Establish an EMEA partner operating rhythm (in partnership with EMEA Partner Alliances) —including business reviews, readiness and capacity assessments, enablement planning, and escalation management—and keep partners current on regional priorities, market dynamics, customer needs, and product and go-to-market changes.

  • Maintain operational hygiene and data integrity for partner-led projects and programs across internal systems, reporting, and workflows; translate feedback from European partners and customers into actionable recommendations for Ironclad teams.

  • A scalable EMEA partner-first operating model and a clear, consistent operating rhythm.

  • Better alignment between partner strategy and qualified deal motions, with greater confidence in partner fit, readiness, and implementation approach before kickoff.

  • More predictable partner capacity and targeted capability plans, with priority enablement gaps owned and closed.

  • Consistent, high-quality partner-led and co-delivered services, with clear roles across EA, Sales, Alliances, Services, Customer Value, and partners.

  • Improved customer time to value, adoption, sustained usage, and expansion outcomes, with a positive contribution to adoption health, GRR, and NDR-oriented outcomes.

What we're looking for:

  • Strong relationship-building, influencing, and communication skills, including the ability to work with senior stakeholders across functions and geographies and turn complex considerations into clear recommendations.

  • Comfort using data and KPIs to evaluate program effectiveness and improve conversion, delivery quality, adoption, and customer outcomes.

  • Experience with change management, adoption planning, or value realisation is strongly preferred; understanding how to set partners up across sales, delivery, enablement, integrations, and customer outcomes is important.

Engagement Manager - Mid-Market Corporates
raw.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

About the Role

The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an Engagement Manager to own adoption across a portfolio of mid-market corporate clients and help their in-house legal teams fundamentally change the way they work.

This is a role for someone who has led change inside complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of 15 – 20 corporate accounts: building the relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser who turns Legora into an embedded part of how those teams operate.

Mid-market means breadth as well as depth. You will be running adoption programmes across 15 – 20 accounts at once, each with its own stakeholders, timelines and success measures, which makes this a role where strong project management is not a nice-to-have but the thing that determines whether you succeed. You will lean on repeatable playbooks where they work and go bespoke where an account earns it.

At the heart of the role is designing each client's adoption playbook and delivering the change programmes that transform how they work. For every account you will build a tailored roadmap, sequence initiatives from initial rollout through function-wide scaled adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class adoption programme at Legora, helping clients realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work.

What You'll Do

You'll lead the post-sale customer experience, owning onboarding, adoption and long-term value realisation for a portfolio of 15 – 20 mid-market corporates. Specifically, you will:

  • Design each client's adoption playbook: the tailored change-management approach, stakeholder map and target outcomes for how that legal function adopts Legora and transforms the way it works.

  • Execute against that playbook, sequencing initiatives from initial rollout to function- and enterprise-wide scaled adoption and adapting as the client's needs and Legora's capabilities evolve.

  • Run those programmes in parallel across the full portfolio, holding the plan, the milestones and the risks for every account and knowing at any moment which ones need your attention this week.

  • Act as a strategic adviser who deeply understands in-house legal priorities — cost, cycle time, risk and doing more without adding headcount — surfaces high-impact opportunities and guides teams towards maximum value from Legora.

  • Drive sustained value through a structured operating cadence: success plans, enablement, stakeholder check-ins, training and value reviews.

  • Orchestrate engagement from cross-functional teams to accelerate client success (GTM, Product, Legal Engineering, Engineering, Marketing, Support), maintaining end-to-end account context and coordination.

  • Partner with GTM on key commercial moments to ensure seamless transitions, continuity and exceptional customer experience, and to identify and realise expansion opportunities.

  • Translate customer feedback into action by collaborating closely with Product, Engineering and Marketing to inform roadmap, positioning and enablement.

  • Build reusable playbooks, templates and enablement material from what works, so the whole Engagement team gets better as you go rather than every account starting from scratch.

What You Bring

You care deeply about customer outcomes and you know that transformation has to be designed and led. You're proactive, strategic and comfortable steering demanding, senior stakeholders through significant change. You take pride in being the reason customers adopt, grow and succeed.

We're looking for:

  • A minimum of 5 years' experience in management consulting, legal, LegalTech or customer success in an AI-native B2B vertical.

  • Experience overseeing complex rollouts and adoption programmes at corporates is very desirable. We want someone who has taken a new way of working into a large in-house function, navigated procurement, IT, security and sceptical stakeholders, and made it stick.

  • A strong project management skillset. This is central to the role: with 15 – 20 live programmes you need to be organised by instinct, comfortable holding many threads at once and able to tell the difference between an account that is quiet and an account that is drifting.

  • A consulting or transformation background, with a demonstrated track record of designing and delivering change-management programmes inside complex organisations.

  • Experience building tailored, client-level transformation roadmaps and adoption plans and steering them to measurable outcomes.

  • A track record of driving adoption, retention and satisfaction with corporate clients and senior stakeholders.

  • Experience working with legal, compliance or other regulated and complex industries or the ability to learn a complex domain exceptionally fast.

  • Excellent communication skills — written, verbal and interpersonal. You can hold a conversation with a General Counsel and roll up your sleeves with the hands-on teams who use the product every day.

  • High EQ: you know when to listen, when to advise and when to act.

  • A love of fast-paced, early-stage environments where you help build the playbook, not just follow it.

  • Fluency with metrics and driven by data, customer health and outcomes over process.

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

raw.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

What You'll Do

This role will report into the Strategic Accounts Engagement Director to ensure that a number of our major law firm clients are receiving consistently high client service, and that they are constantly finding value in Legora.

The remit is depth over breadth: a handful of accounts understood thoroughly, where success is measured by whether the partnership is compounding rather than plateauing. This role will also be supported by a dedicated Strategic Account Engagement Associate.

In practice, the work sits closer to embedded change management than to traditional account management. Our clients have already bought the platform. The job is making it land: getting lawyers to change how they work, proving the value back to the partners who signed off, and turning that into the case for the next phase.

Specifically, you will:

  • Act as a key point of contact and strategic advisor. Understand client goals, uncover new use cases, and help our key clients realise maximum value while linking it to ROI.

  • Be available and on hand to end users. Quickly and efficiently discuss use of Legora and potential new use cases.

  • Spend time embedded on client sites, working alongside lawyers where they actually sit. We are looking for someone comfortable working with senior stakeholders, who enjoys spending time with our clients independently, in front of partners and practice heads as well as associates and trainees.

  • Assist the Engagement Director to pinpoint expansion opportunities. You will jointly spearhead the adoption initiatives necessary to realise them.

  • Contribute to the adoption effort practice group by practice group. Discovery sessions, use case validation, drop-ins, enablement. The shape varies by firm and by wave.

  • Monitor customer health metrics in collaboration with the Engagement Associate. Proactively develop and present the Engagement Director with strategies to address any decline in Legora usage, or to sustain momentum from increased adoption.

  • Closely collaborate with Customer Enablement, Product and Marketing. Translate client feedback into actionable insights and product direction to benefit all functions across the organisation. Being a team player is key.

  • Represent Legora in the market. Speaking at events, hosting client sessions, contributing to how our story gets told publicly. Our strongest engagement people are visible in the legal community, not only inside their own accounts.

 

What You Bring

We hire for credibility with lawyers and the commercial instinct to act on what they tell you. That does not come from a single background, and we are open on where yours comes from.

What matters is that you have driven change in a professional services setting: persuading experienced, sceptical, time-poor people to work differently, and making it stick. That might have been inside a law firm, in innovation, change, transformation or business development. It might have been consulting into firms, or at a vendor working alongside them. Having practised law is welcome but is not required.

Beyond that:

  • Three to five years in either:

    • Customer Success or Account Management in a high-growth B2B SaaS environment.

    • Innovation, Change, Transformation or a related role in a law firm or comparable professional services organisation.

  • A track record of driving retention and satisfaction in the enterprise space.

  • Evidence you have changed behaviour, not just managed a relationship.

  • Highly organised. These clients are large and complex, which means competing priorities and requests to keep track of.

  • Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication. You can hold a room of partners, then sit down with a trainee and work through their prompt with them.

  • High EQ and commercial instinct. You know when to listen, when to advise, and when to act.

  • A love of fast-paced, early-stage environments where priorities can shift rapidly and you adapt with them.

  • Comfortable with metrics. Driven by data, customer health and outcomes over process.

Importantly, you are someone who enjoys being in the office five days a week, with onsite client time in the UK and abroad.

Advantageous system skills: Legora, Hex, Pitch, Notion, Salesforce.

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

About the role

You're the local face of People at Legora: bringing local expertise, judgement and a strong understanding of employment practices to support employees and managers through a range of people matters. You will provide local advisory support, run local casework from start to finish, fill process and policy gaps, and make sure the employee experience in your market is accurate, timely and well handled. This is a hands-on, operational role and a strong launchpad for your next step. You'll be close enough to the business to understand how each function really works, trusted to make real judgment calls on the ground, and sharp enough to know when something needs a specialist instead. Sitting within People Operations, you will act as an escalation for our People Operations Specialists, providing guidance and resolving matters that require local interpretation, judgement or a more tailored approach

You'll partner closely with Employee Relations & Compliance, who own our jurisdictional frameworks, create consistent standards, and provide specialist expertise for complex, contested or legally sensitive matters. You'll also work alongside our People Business Partners, sharing local insights and supporting the effective delivery of people initiatives and organisational changes within your local market.


What you'll own

  • Provide practical advice to employees, managers and People Operations colleagues on local employment practices, policies and people matters that require interpretation or judgement.

  • Running local cases from start to finish within the scope of your certification, including absence management, ongoing performance concerns and restructuring conversations, with each one properly scoped, documented and closed

  • Handling intake for leave, accommodation and absence requests, resolving what's routine and recognizing what needs to go further

  • Building out local process and policy, and ensuring people programs effectively land in your market.

  • Identify opportunities to improve local processes, employee experiences and ways of working, collaborating with other People teams to implement improvements.

  • Applying your market's jurisdiction playbook accurately and consistently, and flagging where it doesn't fit local reality

  • Recognizing the moment a matter becomes formal, contested or legally sensitive, and handing it off the same day with everything the next person needs to pick it up seamlessly

  • Keeping your certification and calibration current so your casework meets the same standard as every other market

  • Work closely with People Business Partners and Employee Relations & Compliance, sharing local trends, recurring issues and emerging risks to inform broader people decisions and improvements.


What success looks like

  • Employees and managers get fast, consistent, local support without having to wait on anyone

  • Every case you run is well documented and would stand up to close scrutiny

  • Handoffs are clean and immediate, and nothing formal or legally sensitive stays with you longer than it should

  • Patterns you spot locally, such as a recurring issue or a risk building in one team, are raised early with both Employee Relations & Compliance and the relevant People Partner, before they become bigger problems

  • You're a trusted, visible presence in your market: the person people choose to go to, not a channel they're told to use


Who you are

  • Experience in an HR, People Operations or HR generalist role, ideally with some exposure to employee relations casework

  • A good understanding of local employment practices, employee relations and HR policies, with the ability to apply these in real-world situations.

  • Able to stay neutral and steady under pressure, including with senior stakeholders

  • Sound judgment on when to act and when to escalate; you'd rather flag early than guess

  • Organized and detail-oriented, with documentation clear enough that someone else could pick it up cold

  • Motivated by where this role can lead, with a genuine interest in growing

  • Comfortable working within a defined playbook while bringing your own judgment to how it's applied

About the Role


The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an experienced Engagement Manager to own Legora's global relationship with one of the Big 4, one of our most significant partnerships, and to fundamentally change the way that firm works with Legora.

This is a role for someone who has led change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of this client globally: building the relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser and orchestrator who turns Legora into an embedded part of how their teams operate.

Global means global. You will set the strategy for how the firm adopts Legora worldwide, and Engagement Managers in other regions will run their local programmes against the direction and decisions you set. Day to day, you will be the point of contact for the firm's UK and Ireland practice from our London office, and you will travel regularly to other
member firms in the network to build those relationships and land the programme on the ground. Expect to be travelling around 25% of the time.

At the heart of the role is designing the client's adoption playbook and delivering a multi-year change-management programme that transforms how they work. You will build the roadmap, sequence initiatives from initial rollout through firm-wide scaled adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class adoption programme at Legora, helping the client realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work.

What You'll Do


You'll own the global relationship end to end, leading the post-sale experience across every member firm we work with. Specifically, you will:


● Set the global adoption strategy for the account and lead its execution across regions. Engagement Managers in other markets will deliver their local programmes against the strategy and decisions you set, and you will be accountable for coherence and outcomes globally.
● Act as the primary point of contact for the firm's UK and Ireland practice, while travelling frequently to other member firms to build senior relationships and support local delivery in person.
● Design the client's adoption playbook: the tailored change-management approach, stakeholder map and target outcomes for how the firm adopts Legora and transforms the way it works.
● Execute against that playbook, sequencing initiatives from initial rollout to enterprise-wide scaled adoption and adapting as the client's needs and Legora's capabilities evolve.
● Act as a strategic adviser who deeply understands the client's goals and legal and professional services workflows, surfaces high-impact opportunities and guides teams towards maximum value from Legora.
● Drive sustained value through a structured operating cadence: success plans, enablement, stakeholder check-ins, training and value reviews.
● Orchestrate engagement from cross-functional teams to accelerate client success (GTM, Product, Legal Engineering, Engineering, Marketing, Support), maintaining end-to-end account context and coordination globally.
● Partner with GTM on key commercial moments to ensure seamless transitions, continuity and exceptional customer experience, and to identify and realise expansion opportunities across the account.

raw.title: Senior QA Associate
raw.description:
Your mission

  • Provide experienced QA support and oversight to MeiraGTx operations.
  • Ensure QA regulatory compliance and product quality requirements are met at all times, as well as facilitating product release in a timely manner. 
  • Coach and train the QA team and other functions and continuously improve the local Quality system and provide training & support for Quality relevant systems. 


Job Description

Major Activities and Responsibilities:

  • Provide QA oversight to the manufacturing operation and supporting functions.
  • Management of the MeiraGTx Quality Management System.
  • Generation, Review and approval of relevant GMP documentation. 
  • Create and Review QA Processes. Create/review Standard Operating Procedures, Policies and Training material.
  • Maintain QA KPI metrics.
  • Collaborate with Operational areas, supporting the Team Lead to manage the day-to-day QA Operations.
  • Review Batch documentation and support QA team review of Batch documentation. Ensuring timely and adequate release of GMP compliant product in accordance with Regulatory and site-specific authorisations.
  • Manage and support QA team Facility Walk rounds and QA support for all operational areas.
  • Provide direct quality team support during customer and regulatory audits.
  • Perform internal audits and inspections and audit write up.
  • Quality Systems: Complete Reporting, reviewing, investigating, root cause analysis, assessing Quality Risk Assessments, Incidents, Deviations, CAPA’s, OOS, Change Controls and temperature excursions.
  • Support Document Management activities when required.
  • Proactively initiate and support continuous improvement of the Quality Management System.
  • Deliver compliance training to operational areas.
  • Provide guidance and assistance to quality related issues in Operational areas and to External third parties.
  • Deputise for the QA Team Leader – Operations when required.
  • Proactive individual,  able to step in without being asked. Identifies upcoming activities or tasks and works on completion without the need to be asked.
  • Collaboration and stakeholder management.
  • Adaptability ad resilience.
  • Supports innovation by challenging outdated practices and encouraging better ways of working.
  • Always asks and understands the “why” and is capable of explaining this to others. Does not automatically accept the status quo.
  • Finds better ways for completing existing activities/processes saving time or effort while remaining compliant.
  • Data driven decision making. Able to check reliability of sources, identify gaps, inconsistencies or misleading information.
  • Demonstrates critical thinking and logical reasoning. 

Key Job Competencies and Behaviours
  • Minimum 5 years experience of working within a sterile GMP manufacturing environment.
  • Excellent understanding of Quality Management Systems.
  • Demonstrate very good understanding of the purpose of the regulation requirements in terms of how they translate to product quality and patient safety.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and experience in database use and eQMS systems.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills. Role model for professional behaviours, respectful relationships, positive and constructive communication.
  • Capable of demonstrating structured thinking, data gathering and analysis for informed decisions.
  • Good organisational and time management skills and able to demonstrate flexibility and adaptability. Capable of consistent on-time delivery of their individual tasks and responsibilities. Able to prioritise workload, decisive thinker able to work within agreed timescales.
  • A high level of attention to detail.
  • Good team player and must also be able to work independently.
  • Strong experience in Regulatory inspections and Client audits.

Job Background
  • Experience working in a Sterile manufacturing GMP environment including a minimum 5 years’ experience in Compliance and Quality Assurance.
  • IT literate, experience managing and operating an electronic QMS.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

raw.title: Forward Deployed Consultant
raw.description:
monday.com is the AI work platform powering the most ambitious teams. 250,000+ customers across departments use us to bring people, workflows, and AI agents together on one flexible platform where AI doesn't just assist, it executes. We move fast, build things that matter, and foster an ownership-driven culture where you're empowered to shape how organisations work and outpace their competition.

Our team is growing and we are looking for a Forward Deployed Consultant to join our Professional Services team! In this role, you will train, advise and consult, and build with customers to optimize their use of the monday.com AI work platform during the course of an AI transformation, implementation, or ongoing managed services engagement. You will design and build the AI-native solutions that get them there, from intelligent workflows and agents to the automations and reporting their business relies on. You will run engagements both independently and as a part of a delivery team collaborating with deployment strategists and engineers.

Please note that this is a hybrid position with three days/week in our London office.

About the Role

  • Lead AI transformation and implementation engagements for monday.com customers, designing and building tailored solutions using agents, vibe-coded applications, and other advanced capabilities of the monday AI work platform.

  • Build strong relationships with client stakeholders, running the discovery that uncovers their desired business outcomes, and ensure successful adoption of the solutions you deliver across their organization.

  • Consult on business process design, mapping how work moves through a customer's organization and recommending the process changes that should be made before the solution is built.

  • Design sophisticated workflows and relational data structures within the monday.com platform to solve complex business cases, partnering with technical resources for data conversions, integrations, and agentic engineering.

  • Actively leverage monday AI and external Generative/Agentic AI tools to accelerate solution design, automate complex business logic, and deliver intelligent workflows for our customers.

  • Act as the project manager on standalone engagements, building and executing on project plans that ensure deliverables stay on-time and on-budget, and delivering defined scope alongside a deployment strategist on larger ones.

  • Run online webinars, training sessions, consultations, and one-on-one demos that show customers how our product capabilities translate into business value.

  • Produce the documentation, walkthroughs, and exit artifacts for your engagements that allow customers to operate, maintain, and extend what you built independently.

  • Represent the voice of the customer by advocating for their needs and influencing the product development roadmap.

  • Contribute the patterns and reusable assets you develop in the field back to our shared asset library.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience as a forward-deployed consultant, implementation consultant, solutions consultant, or technical project manager in enterprise software.

  • Experience leading software implementation or managed services projects that required hands-on build and system configuration in project management, CRM, service desk, or collaborative work management software.

  • Fluency in Generative and Agentic AI tools, with a strong understanding of how to leverage AI in streamlining work productivity and building intelligent workflows and agents.

  • Familiarity with what keeps AI reliable in production, including human review, checking outputs, and knowing when a deterministic automation is the better answer.

  • Strong problem solving skills, rooted in computational thinking, systems design, and an understanding of relational data structures.

  • Business process design and consulting experience, with the business acumen to frame an engagement around customer outcomes, and the judgment to read the implicit problem behind an explicit request.

  • Working knowledge of integration platforms (make.com, Zapier) sufficient to configure lightweight integrations yourself, with foundational knowledge of APIs (GraphQL) and MCP a plus.

  • Strong customer-facing and presentation skills with the ability to establish credibility with client stakeholders and executives, and to clearly articulate technical topics to a non-technical audience.

  • Ability to rapidly learn and take advantage of new concepts, business models, and technologies across a changing set of customers and industries.

  • Detail-oriented with strong project management skills, comfortable running engagements independently and working across several at once.

  • Superb written and verbal communication skills, with a positive attitude, empathy, high energy, and the ability to take initiative and adapt.

  • Willingness to travel up to 20% of the time.

  • BA or BS degree preferred.


Please note that this role is hybrid.

Visa sponsorship for this role is currently not available.

We hire talented individuals, regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, ancestry, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, military or veteran status, cultural background, religious beliefs, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

With a vibrant team of over 500 professionals across North America and Europe, and offices in Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, Pigment has successfully secured nearly $400 million in funding from leading global venture capitalists. At Pigment, we champion smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo—all as a united team. Every team member has the opportunity to make a significant impact and tackle ambitious challenges. Together, we pursue excellence with a collaborative spirit, continuously raising the bar to ensure strong performance and a proactive approach while fostering an environment of humility.  
 
If you are passionate about innovation and wish to collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry, we would love to hear from you!

 
🚀 The Opportunity:
 
As a Fullstack Software Engineer you’ll work on performance-critical systems that process and aggregate millions of records in real time, directly enabling our clients to make better, faster decisions. Your role will be mostly working on backend in C#, with some frontend in React.
 
Here’s why this is an exciting opportunity:
 
✨ Work on the Core Engine: Contribute to the design and optimization of our proprietary formula and query engine.
⚙️ Solve Complex Problems: Tackle scalability and performance challenges across high-volume, real-time datasets.
🧠 Shape the Product: Collaborate closely with frontend engineers and product managers to deliver impactful features.
🚀 Own the Stack: Build and maintain backend services using modern technologies like .NET Core, PostgreSQL, React, and GCP.

Our Engineering team

Pigment engineers participate in the entire application development lifecycle, focusing on design, coding and keeping the production platform up and running. They can be specialized, but there is no strict separation between the backend and the frontend.

Who you are

- Proven experience designing object oriented software with languages such as C#, Java, C++, Golang, Rust, Python or Ruby (this list is not exhaustive).
- Proven experience with JavaScript, CSS and JavaScript libraries or frameworks such as React, Vue.js or Angular.
- Great team spirit with a problem-solving attitude.

raw.title: Datacentre Operations Engineer
raw.description:
About Us

Radiant is powered intelligence, delivering scalable, high-performance compute infrastructure purpose-built for AI and HPC workloads. Operating across global data centres, we run mission-critical environments where uptime, throughput, and ultra-low latency are non-negotiable.

Role Overview

We are seeking a deeply technical, hardware-passionate Datacentre Operations Engineer to execute on-the-ground operations for our new East London deployment—Radiant's newest AI infrastructure site. This role focuses on delivering precise, repeatable physical practices—including advanced smart-hands support, complex cabling, and hands-on operation of high-density, air-cooled compute systems—to guarantee world-class SLAs on next-generation hardware architecture.

Working closely with Infrastructure (HPC) SRE, Network Engineering, and Datacentre Strategy teams, you will uphold uncompromising standards across East London's data centre floor, spanning multiple data halls. You will live and breathe the hardware, maintaining elite facility reliability through hands-on deployment, proactive maintenance, rapid incident response, and structured break/fix execution across high-density air cooling systems, busbar-based power distribution, and next-generation GPU compute platforms. The role centres on technical execution and optimised output.

You will turn global engineering standards into flawless, repeatable daily routines, continually honing on-the-ground practices to keep our most advanced hardware running at peak performance. East London's hardware platform is NVIDIA B300-class, fully air-cooled compute, delivered through a new OEM partner being onboarded to Radiant's fleet; while the interfaces and overall architecture closely align with other OEM platforms you may already know, you'll be one of the first teams operating it on the ground, so a fast learning curve and strong first-principles troubleshooting matter more than prior exposure to this specific vendor.

You will be part of the founding team standing up 24x7x365 on-site coverage at East London to meet tight customer SLAs, and as Radiant expands its EMEA footprint, your relentless drive for hardware perfection and proven field expertise with high-density environments will serve as the operational blueprint to scale execution models efficiently across the region.

What’s in it for you?

Join a team operating some of the world’s most advanced high-performance computing infrastructure. As a Datacentre Operations Engineer, you’ll work hands-on with cutting-edge GPU and CPU platforms — including the latest NVIDIA architectures — powering dense, large-scale compute environments used for AI, machine learning, and next-generation workloads.

This is an opportunity to build expertise at the forefront of modern infrastructure, where reliability, scale, and performance matter every day. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers across a globally distributed organisation that values openness, inclusion, technical excellence, and continuous learning.

We move quickly, solve meaningful challenges, and give people the space to make an impact. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy working with advanced technology, and want to help shape the future of high-performance compute, you’ll find both challenge and opportunity here.

You can also expect:

  • Exposure to industry-leading GPU and AI infrastructure

  • Opportunities to grow alongside a rapidly scaling global business

  • A collaborative, inclusive, and supportive engineering culture

  • Real ownership and the ability to influence operational excellence

  • Work that sits at the intersection of people, performance, and technology

  • A modern, flexible, globally connected workplace with ambitious goals

Key Responsibilities

Hardware Operations & Break/Fix

  • Quickly diagnose and resolve hardware and network issues to maximise uptime; execute structured fault isolation methodologies to drive rapid resolution

  • Respond to critical hardware alerts via our monitoring and observability platform; contribute to ongoing service improvement to improve monitoring capability and alert quality

  • Deploy and maintain HPC and AI hardware for uninterrupted operations, including hardware troubleshooting, firmware updates, and component replacement

  • Execute break/fix procedures for advanced hardware platforms, including GPU module exchange, component-level fault isolation, and firmware-level diagnostics

  • Execute or support break/fix operations on ultra-high-density compute systems including NVIDIA B300-class chassis or equivalent platforms, including GPU/fan module exchange, chassis-level fault isolation, and busbar connection/disconnection—under the direction of the Lead where qualification is in progress

Air Cooling Operations

  • Operate, monitor, and maintain high-density air cooling infrastructure in conjunction with our datacentre partner, including CRAC/CRAH units, in-row and containment cooling, and associated airflow management systems

  • Facilitate in conjunction with our datacentre partner, routine and corrective maintenance on air cooling systems: monitoring supply/return temperatures and airflow rates, maintaining hot-aisle/cold-aisle containment and blanking, and performing scheduled filter and component inspections

  • Follow and contribute to SOPs for safe working around high-density, air-cooled compute platforms

  • Monitor thermal performance and raise anomalies before they escalate into incidents

Capacity Management

  • Contribute to site-level capacity management operations, maintaining accurate records of power, space, and cooling utilisation

  • Support capacity planning activities by providing accurate as-built data and flagging infrastructure changes to the Lead and relevant teams

  • Manage on-the-ground assets from point of purchase and delivery through lifecycle management and disposal, owning asset management within Radiant's CMDB system

Infrastructure & Facilities

  • Handle RMAs and support requests within Radiant's Service Level Objectives (SLOs) to meet customer contract SLAs

  • Contribute to ongoing maintenance, fostering compliance and leveraging strong vendor partnerships

  • Operate cooling, power distribution (including busbar and PDU infrastructure), and other critical data centre technologies to maintain high operational standards

  • Develop and maintain datacentre/hardware management SOPs, ensuring continual alignment with Radiant's governance and compliance requirements

Service & Operational Excellence

  • Apply ITSM frameworks: Incident, Major Incident, Change Management, and service improvement

  • Operate and support services 24x7x365 for production environments as part of a structured on-site shift rotation—working 12-hour shifts across a 4-team pattern with two engineers on shift at all times—to meet tight customer SLAs

  • Prioritise and triage incident and smart-hands workload ensuring tight SLA coverage is maintained with a small on the ground team

  • Contribute to Incident postmortem analyses, root cause analysis, document learnings, and automate remediations

  • Communicate technical decisions clearly to stakeholders and customers

  • Champion a culture of: do, document, automate

  • Willing to cross train and upskill in Infrastructure/Platform SRE practices

  • Willing to travel across EMEA to support future datacentre onboarding and train in new technologies

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Degree in Computer Science/Electrical Engineering, or 5+ years of directly relevant industry experience in data centre operations

  • 3+ years of experience in data centre operations, HPC, or related roles

  • Passion for hardware and upholding the highest operational standards on the ground

  • Strong communication skills in English

  • Proven hands-on experience with HPC/NVIDIA GPU platforms or equivalent high-density compute systems, high-performance storage, and networking

  • Practical knowledge of high-density air cooling systems—CRAC/CRAH operation, airflow and thermal monitoring, containment management, and associated maintenance—or strong related cooling infrastructure experience

  • Experience with, or demonstrable willingness and aptitude to train on, ultra-high-density compute platforms such as NVIDIA B300, busbar-based power distribution, or equivalent systems

  • Experience with and passion for management of compute at massive scale

  • Comfort operating a newly-onboarded OEM hardware platform, applying transferable knowledge from other high-density GPU/HPC OEM systems to ramp up quickly without direct prior exposure to this specific vendor

  • Familiarity with structured break/fix practices for complex hardware platforms, including module-level component exchange and firmware fault isolation

  • Expertise in hardware installation, network configuration, and low-level system maintenance, including firmware management

  • Knowledge of data centre environment technologies, including cooling and high-density power distribution

  • Understanding of capacity management principles: power, space, and cooling tracking

  • Strong understanding of hardware and spares management; ability to handle RMAs within defined SLOs

  • Understanding of HPC and AI workloads at a high level

  • Strong problem-solving abilities and resilience in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong grasp of ITSM and service operation best practices

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate with cross-functional, internationally dispersed teams

  • Comfortable interfacing with internal stakeholders and external customers

  • Bonus: Vendor-endorsed qualifications from NVIDIA or equivalent OEMs for high-density, air-cooled AI compute systems

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of large scale private cloud deployments and capacity planning.

  • Qualifications in HVAC management and deployments

  • Certifications in relevant areas - Hardware, Networking

  • ITIL Foundation level qualification or equivalent experience

You will turn global engineering standards into flawless, repeatable daily routines, continually honing on-the-ground practices to keep our most advanced hardware running at peak performance. East London's hardware platform is NVIDIA B300-class, fully air-cooled compute, delivered through a new OEM partner being onboarded to Radiant's fleet; while the interfaces and overall architecture closely align with other OEM platforms you may already know, you'll be one of the first teams operating it on the ground, so a fast learning curve and strong first-principles troubleshooting matter more than prior exposure to this specific vendor.

You will be part of the founding team standing up 24x7x365 on-site coverage at East London to meet tight customer SLAs, and as Radiant expands its EMEA footprint, your relentless drive for hardware perfection and proven field expertise with high-density environments will serve as the operational blueprint to scale execution models efficiently across the region.

What’s in it for you?

Join a team operating some of the world’s most advanced high-performance computing infrastructure. As a Datacentre Operations Engineer, you’ll work hands-on with cutting-edge GPU and CPU platforms — including the latest NVIDIA architectures — powering dense, large-scale compute environments used for AI, machine learning, and next-generation workloads.

This is an opportunity to build expertise at the forefront of modern infrastructure, where reliability, scale, and performance matter every day. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers across a globally distributed organisation that values openness, inclusion, technical excellence, and continuous learning.

We move quickly, solve meaningful challenges, and give people the space to make an impact. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy working with advanced technology, and want to help shape the future of high-performance compute, you’ll find both challenge and opportunity here.

You can also expect:

  • Exposure to industry-leading GPU and AI infrastructure

  • Opportunities to grow alongside a rapidly scaling global business

  • A collaborative, inclusive, and supportive engineering culture

  • Real ownership and the ability to influence operational excellence

  • Work that sits at the intersection of people, performance, and technology

  • A modern, flexible, globally connected workplace with ambitious goals

Key Responsibilities

Hardware Operations & Break/Fix

  • Quickly diagnose and resolve hardware and network issues to maximise uptime; execute structured fault isolation methodologies to drive rapid resolution

  • Respond to critical hardware alerts via our monitoring and observability platform; contribute to ongoing service improvement to improve monitoring capability and alert quality

  • Deploy and maintain HPC and AI hardware for uninterrupted operations, including hardware troubleshooting, firmware updates, and component replacement

  • Execute break/fix procedures for advanced hardware platforms, including GPU module exchange, component-level fault isolation, and firmware-level diagnostics

  • Execute or support break/fix operations on ultra-high-density compute systems including NVIDIA B300-class chassis or equivalent platforms, including GPU/fan module exchange, chassis-level fault isolation, and busbar connection/disconnection—under the direction of the Lead where qualification is in progress

Air Cooling Operations

  • Operate, monitor, and maintain high-density air cooling infrastructure in conjunction with our datacentre partner, including CRAC/CRAH units, in-row and containment cooling, and associated airflow management systems

  • Facilitate in conjunction with our datacentre partner, routine and corrective maintenance on air cooling systems: monitoring supply/return temperatures and airflow rates, maintaining hot-aisle/cold-aisle containment and blanking, and performing scheduled filter and component inspections

  • Follow and contribute to SOPs for safe working around high-density, air-cooled compute platforms

  • Monitor thermal performance and raise anomalies before they escalate into incidents

Capacity Management

  • Contribute to site-level capacity management operations, maintaining accurate records of power, space, and cooling utilisation

  • Support capacity planning activities by providing accurate as-built data and flagging infrastructure changes to the Lead and relevant teams

  • Manage on-the-ground assets from point of purchase and delivery through lifecycle management and disposal, owning asset management within Radiant's CMDB system

Infrastructure & Facilities

  • Handle RMAs and support requests within Radiant's Service Level Objectives (SLOs) to meet customer contract SLAs

  • Contribute to ongoing maintenance, fostering compliance and leveraging strong vendor partnerships

  • Operate cooling, power distribution (including busbar and PDU infrastructure), and other critical data centre technologies to maintain high operational standards

  • Develop and maintain datacentre/hardware management SOPs, ensuring continual alignment with Radiant's governance and compliance requirements

Service & Operational Excellence

  • Apply ITSM frameworks: Incident, Major Incident, Change Management, and service improvement

  • Operate and support services 24x7x365 for production environments as part of a structured on-site shift rotation—working 12-hour shifts across a 4-team pattern with two engineers on shift at all times—to meet tight customer SLAs

  • Prioritise and triage incident and smart-hands workload ensuring tight SLA coverage is maintained with a small on the ground team

  • Contribute to Incident postmortem analyses, root cause analysis, document learnings, and automate remediations

  • Communicate technical decisions clearly to stakeholders and customers

  • Champion a culture of: do, document, automate

  • Willing to cross train and upskill in Infrastructure/Platform SRE practices

  • Willing to travel across EMEA to support future datacentre onboarding and train in new technologies

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Degree in Computer Science/Electrical Engineering, or 5+ years of directly relevant industry experience in data centre operations

  • 3+ years of experience in data centre operations, HPC, or related roles

  • Passion for hardware and upholding the highest operational standards on the ground

  • Strong communication skills in English

  • Proven hands-on experience with HPC/NVIDIA GPU platforms or equivalent high-density compute systems, high-performance storage, and networking

  • Practical knowledge of high-density air cooling systems—CRAC/CRAH operation, airflow and thermal monitoring, containment management, and associated maintenance—or strong related cooling infrastructure experience

  • Experience with, or demonstrable willingness and aptitude to train on, ultra-high-density compute platforms such as NVIDIA B300, busbar-based power distribution, or equivalent systems

  • Experience with and passion for management of compute at massive scale

  • Comfort operating a newly-onboarded OEM hardware platform, applying transferable knowledge from other high-density GPU/HPC OEM systems to ramp up quickly without direct prior exposure to this specific vendor

  • Familiarity with structured break/fix practices for complex hardware platforms, including module-level component exchange and firmware fault isolation

  • Expertise in hardware installation, network configuration, and low-level system maintenance, including firmware management

  • Knowledge of data centre environment technologies, including cooling and high-density power distribution

  • Understanding of capacity management principles: power, space, and cooling tracking

  • Strong understanding of hardware and spares management; ability to handle RMAs within defined SLOs

  • Understanding of HPC and AI workloads at a high level

  • Strong problem-solving abilities and resilience in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong grasp of ITSM and service operation best practices

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate with cross-functional, internationally dispersed teams

  • Comfortable interfacing with internal stakeholders and external customers

  • Bonus: Vendor-endorsed qualifications from NVIDIA or equivalent OEMs for high-density, air-cooled AI compute systems

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of large scale private cloud deployments and capacity planning.

  • Qualifications in HVAC management and deployments

  • Certifications in relevant areas - Hardware, Networking

  • ITIL Foundation level qualification or equivalent experience

raw.title: Engineering Manager
raw.description:
About the role

Radiant exists to redefine how AI infrastructure is built and operated at scale. We are creating a vertically integrated AI platform that brings together physical infrastructure, control planes, and cloud-native software to deliver abundance, control, and sovereignty in a world constrained by traditional hyperscaler models.

Our vision is to enable organisations to build, train, and deploy AI at national and global scale without surrendering control over performance, cost, or locality. This requires engineering systems that operate across software, hardware, and physical environments, and that remain reliable as scale and complexity increase.

We are scaling our engineering organisation now. Most of our engineering manager seats are open. You join, shape how the teams work, and grow with them.

As an Engineering Manager, you lead a team building and operating core parts of Radiant's cloud platform. You combine people leadership, technical judgement, delivery ownership and cross-functional collaboration. You work closely with product, infrastructure, SRE, security and other engineering teams.

This is a hands-on leadership role. It focuses on building strong teams, delivering reliable platform capabilities, and creating an environment where engineers do their best work.

The streams

We run engineering as ten streams in three groups. Each stream is a full team of about nine people: principal, senior and mid-level software engineers, an SDET, a DevOps engineer and a platform engineer. Each stream has its own engineering manager.

  • Infrastructure: Compute, Network, Storage, Cluster

  • Platform: Cloud, Infra, Observability, Security

  • AI: Training, Inference

You do not apply for a single stream. We hire strong managers first. Then we agree your stream with you, based on your strengths and interests. Your first stream is a starting point, not a fixed track. Moves between streams are normal here.

Key responsibilities

You lead one stream end to end: people, delivery and production.

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of about nine engineers across platform, infrastructure and distributed systems.

  • Own team execution across planning, prioritisation, delivery, quality and operational readiness.

  • Partner with product to turn priorities into clear technical plans and achievable milestones.

  • Provide technical leadership on architecture, reliability, scalability and engineering trade-offs.

  • Set strong engineering practices for design, testing, observability, documentation and incident learning.

  • Improve team effectiveness through clear ownership, healthy processes and strong cross-team collaboration.

  • Hire, onboard and retain high-performing engineers. Hiring is a large part of the first year. Expect around two hours a day on it.

  • Support career development through regular feedback, coaching and progression planning.

  • Manage technical risk, dependencies and delivery challenges across complex platform initiatives.

  • Bring AI-assisted engineering into daily work, within our guardrails.

  • Build a culture of ownership, pragmatism, operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Attitude comes first

  • Curiosity: you learn new domains fast. GPUs, networks and storage excite you rather than worry you.

  • Candour: you say what you think, with care. You welcome challenge to your own ideas.

  • Builder mindset: much here is not built yet. You enjoy creating the process, not just running it.

  • Pace with standards: you move fast and keep quality high.

  • Generosity: you make the people around you better. You give credit and share what you know.

Your profile

  • Experience leading engineering teams building cloud platforms, infrastructure, developer tooling or distributed systems.

  • A strong technical background. You engage credibly in architecture and design discussions.

  • A good understanding of:

    • Cloud infrastructure: compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes, containers

    • Platform engineering: APIs, automation, IAM, observability, reliability

    • Distributed systems: scaling, consistency, failure handling

    • Engineering operations: incident response, capacity, performance, production ownership

  • Proven experience in people management, hiring, coaching and performance development.

  • Strong delivery and prioritisation skills across competing priorities.

  • Comfort working closely with product and other engineering leaders in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.

  • The ability to balance technical quality, delivery speed, reliability and team sustainability.

Experience with GPU, HPC or AI infrastructure is a bonus. Nobody has depth in every area above. Tell us which you know and which you want to learn.

What you bring

  • People leadership: you build strong teams and help engineers grow.

  • Technical judgement: you challenge designs and guide trade-offs without owning every implementation detail.

  • Execution: you create clarity and drive complex work to completion.

  • Systems thinking: you understand how platform components and teams fit together.

  • Operational mindset: you care about reliability, maintainability and production quality.

  • Ownership: you take responsibility for both team health and engineering outcomes.

raw.title: IT Operations Systems Assistant
raw.description:
Reports to: People Manager / Operations team

Location: London / UK preferred (hybrid — office access is a bonus, not required)

Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we're building this organisation from the ground up. We're looking for people who'd rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you've previously managed.

This is a cross-functional role requiring strong technical, commercial, and delivery capabilities, with exposure to executive stakeholders and our EOR and benefits providers, regional legal and finance partners, and every hiring manager relying on one people function as we scale.

What You'll Do

You will provide day-to-day operational and technical support across Radiant's IT systems, hardware, and end users. The role acts as a first point of contact for IT support requests and plays a key part in keeping core systems, devices, and user accounts running smoothly, securely, and in line with company policies.

Key Responsibilities

Service desk and user support

  • Act as first point of contact for IT support requests, logging, triaging, and resolving tickets, escalating to senior colleagues where appropriate

Systems and account administration

  • Administer user accounts through the joiner, mover, and leaver process, including account creation, permission changes, and timely deactivation of access

  • Assign and track software licences, ensuring allocations remain accurate and cost-effective

Hardware and asset management

  • Build, configure, and deploy laptops and mobile devices for new starters

  • Maintain an accurate IT asset register, tracking equipment from procurement through to secure disposal

  • Arrange repairs, replacements, and warranty claims with external suppliers

Security and compliance

  • Perform periodic audits of systems access

  • Support day-to-day security practices, including multi-factor authentication setup, access reviews, and prompt removal of leaver access

  • Follow established IT policies and procedures, and flag risks, incidents, or recurring issues to senior colleagues

  • Handle accounts, access, and company data with care and in line with data protection obligations

Documentation and continuous improvement

  • Create and maintain knowledge base articles, user guides, and internal process documentation

  • Identify recurring issues and contribute suggestions to improve systems, processes, and the end-user experience

Qualities we look for:

  • Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up.

  • Inspire the change: There's no blueprint for the future. You'll embrace challenges and change.

  • You're real and you're true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you'll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you're talking to, you treat everyone the same.

  • Get stuck in: You'd rather be building than overseeing. Our strategy will keep evolving, and so will you — attitude and adaptability matter more to us than a fixed playbook or a big team behind you.

raw.title: Account Executive - Enterprise
raw.description:
This role is based out of our Amsterdam office 🇳🇱 or London office 🇬🇧


We are an office-first company & believe great products are made when we are together.


About Stacks

Stacks is building an AI-native platform that reinvents how modern finance teams run the monthly close. The opportunity is massive: every growing company depends on accurate, timely financial data, yet most are still operating with tools and workflows built for a different era.

In just two years, we’ve grown from a team of 2 to 30+ and are on a rapid trajectory. We’ve raised a $23m Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and we were recently recognised as one of Harmonic’s Hottest Startups of 2026.

We’re already trusted by leading European scale-ups including Pleo, Freetrade, and Motorway. Our team is a blend of finance, product, and technical experts from top-tier companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, Mollie, and Bunq, united by the drive to create a game-changing solution.

We’re a team that is deeply customer-obsessed, plays to win, and isn’t afraid to take big, bold bets. We move fast, hold a high bar, and are committed to growing together as we scale.

About the Role

Stacks is looking for a fiercely ambitious, entrepreneurial, and commercially driven Enterprise Account Executive to join our GTM team!

In this high-impact role, you’ll contribute to creating and executing our GTM strategy at Stacks. If you’re excited by the idea of limitless growth and fast-paced challenges, this is a unique opportunity to accelerate your career as you help shape the future of Stacks.

🧱 What You'll Do

  • Drive Revenue Growth: Own the full sales cycle from outbound prospecting and qualification through to closing and activation. You'll regularly engage with Controllers, VPs of Finance, and CFOs to champion Stacks as the modern close management solution.

  • Consultative & Strategic Selling: Understand each prospect’s financial close pain points and map them Stacks through tailored, value-driven conversations. Displace legacy vendors through strategic positioning

  • Finance Stakeholders: Sell to senior finance decision-makers. You’ll navigate complex org structures and buying processes in the Mid-Market & Enterprise space. Build deep account plans across global organisations

  • Product Mastery: Quickly ramp up on our product and develop a deep understanding of the monthly close workflow.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration: • Act as quarterback across Product, Security, Legal, and CS

  • Expand Our Reach: Build relationships with finance teams across Europe as we expand our presence

  • Make a Strategic Impact: Shape Stacks’ Enterprise GTM motion and field playbooks

🧩 What You Need

  • 4-10 years of SaaS Enterprise Experience: Proven success in a full-cycle, quota-carrying sales role at a high-growth startup or scale-up. You've sold complex B2B SaaS to Mid-Market or Enterprise customers. Repeated six-figure or seven-figure wins

  • Finance SaaS Selling Experience: You’ve sold into the Office of the CFO, ideally, financial reporting, planning, ERP, or close automation tools, and understand how to speak their language.

  • Flawless Sales Execution: You know how to prospect, qualify, run discovery, tailor demos, negotiate, and close. Calm operator in longer sales cycles with political complexity

  • Strong Product Acumen: You're quick to understand complex tools and can explain them in a clear, compelling way that resonates with both finance and technical stakeholders.

  • Entrepreneurial Energy: You’re excited to build from the ground up. You thrive in ambiguity, move fast, and bring structure where needed. Evidence building territories from scratch

  • History of Excellence: A consistent record of exceeding quota and standing out in high-performance environments—whether in business, academics, sports, or other pursuits.

🚀 What’s in It for You

  • Foundational role: Help shape a category-defining company from an early stage, working directly with founders and a small, high-agency team.

  • Meaningful ownership: Competitive equity in a company scaling rapidly towards $10m ARR, where your impact will directly shape the outcome.

  • Cutting-edge product and tech: Work at the intersection of AI and finance, building systems that fundamentally change how companies run their financial close.

  • High-calibre team: Collaborate with people from companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, and Mollie.

  • Exceptional workspace: Our London HQ is based in Fora — a modern, design-led space in the heart of the city with access to a gym, classes, and an environment built for focused, in-person building

  • Strong team culture: We run regular socials and off-sites that bring the team together properly, we recently have our 2-year anniversary party in Amsterdam, with board games, a tarot card reader and live music 🎶

🤝 The Hiring Process

We move fast. Most candidates complete the full process within two weeks

  • Step 1: 30 min intro chat with our TA team to learn more about Stacks and get genuinely excited about what we are building

  • Step 2: 30 min chat with Julien (VP Sales) to dive into your commercial experience

  • Step 3: 45 min deep dive with Anand (Head of Partnerships) into the deals and customers you have worked on

  • Step 4: 30 min chat with Freddie and Will, our AEs. You can ask your burning questions

  • Step 5: 60 min onsite case presentation with the team, focused on a real-life discovery + pitch scenario

  • Step 6: 30 min onsite conversation with our Founder about Stacks culture, values, and the journey ahead

  • Step 7: Offer. If we have gotten this far, we are excited about you and we will make that clear

Stacks is looking for a fiercely ambitious, entrepreneurial, and commercially driven Enterprise Account Executive to join our GTM team!

In this high-impact role, you’ll contribute to creating and executing our GTM strategy at Stacks. If you’re excited by the idea of limitless growth and fast-paced challenges, this is a unique opportunity to accelerate your career as you help shape the future of Stacks.

  • Drive Revenue Growth: Own the full sales cycle from outbound prospecting and qualification through to closing and activation. You'll regularly engage with Controllers, VPs of Finance, and CFOs to champion Stacks as the modern close management solution.
