  • Finance Stakeholders: Sell to senior finance decision-makers. You’ll navigate complex org structures and buying processes in the Mid-Market & Enterprise space. Build deep account plans across global organisations

  • Product Mastery: Quickly ramp up on our product and develop a deep understanding of the monthly close workflow.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration: • Act as quarterback across Product, Security, Legal, and CS

  • Expand Our Reach: Build relationships with finance teams across Europe as we expand our presence

  • Make a Strategic Impact: Shape Stacks’ Enterprise GTM motion and field playbooks

🧩 What You Need

  • 4-10 years of SaaS Enterprise Experience: Proven success in a full-cycle, quota-carrying sales role at a high-growth startup or scale-up. You've sold complex B2B SaaS to Mid-Market or Enterprise customers. Repeated six-figure or seven-figure wins

  • Finance SaaS Selling Experience: You’ve sold into the Office of the CFO, ideally, financial reporting, planning, ERP, or close automation tools, and understand how to speak their language.

  • Flawless Sales Execution: You know how to prospect, qualify, run discovery, tailor demos, negotiate, and close. Calm operator in longer sales cycles with political complexity

  • Strong Product Acumen: You're quick to understand complex tools and can explain them in a clear, compelling way that resonates with both finance and technical stakeholders.

  • Entrepreneurial Energy: You’re excited to build from the ground up. You thrive in ambiguity, move fast, and bring structure where needed. Evidence building territories from scratch

  • History of Excellence: A consistent record of exceeding quota and standing out in high-performance environments—whether in business, academics, sports, or other pursuits.

🚀 What’s in It for You

  • Foundational role: Help shape a category-defining company from an early stage, working directly with founders and a small, high-agency team.

  • Meaningful ownership: Competitive equity in a company scaling rapidly towards $10m ARR, where your impact will directly shape the outcome.

  • Cutting-edge product and tech: Work at the intersection of AI and finance, building systems that fundamentally change how companies run their financial close.

  • High-calibre team: Collaborate with people from companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, and Mollie.

  • Exceptional workspace: Our London HQ is based in Fora — a modern, design-led space in the heart of the city with access to a gym, classes, and an environment built for focused, in-person building

  • Strong team culture: We run regular socials and off-sites that bring the team together properly, we recently have our 2-year anniversary party in Amsterdam, with board games, a tarot card reader and live music 🎶

We move fast. Most candidates complete the full process within two weeks

  • Step 1: 30 min intro chat with our TA team to learn more about Stacks and get genuinely excited about what we are building

  • Step 2: 30 min chat with Julien (VP Sales) to dive into your commercial experience

  • Step 3: 45 min deep dive with Anand (Head of Partnerships) into the deals and customers you have worked on

  • Step 4: 30 min chat with Freddie and Will, our AEs. You can ask your burning questions

  • Step 6: 30 min onsite conversation with our Founder about Stacks culture, values, and the journey ahead

  • Step 7: Offer. If we have gotten this far, we are excited about you and we will make that clear

raw.title: Clinical AI Lead
raw.description:
About Aptura AI

We work with frontier AI labs and companies across healthcare, finance, and legal providing the specialist knowledge and human oversight that makes AI models more accurate and reliable in these highly regulated domains.

In healthcare, we specialise in sourcing clinicians experts and annotating medical data at scale that is used to train the models such as labelling and reviewing consultation notes, medical images or pathology reports.

The projects we manage tend to sit at the heart of how AI learns to understand real clinical interactions from consultations, workflows, and the delivery of care that directly affects both clinicians and patients. Projects we have been involved in, include SNOMED Medical Coding for Medical Device Registration, AI powered MDT platforms and AI-assisted Clinical Trials Recruitment.

We're a lean, in-person team based in London. We move quickly, hold ourselves to a high standard, and expect every individual to contribute directly.

About the role

As a second hire in the healthcare team it comes with a lot of responsibility and growth opportunities. The role involves staying up to date with the latest published literature for AI in healthcare. You will play a key role in designing and publishing benchmarks in collaboration with stakeholders. It also involves being a part of initial customer conversations and sourcing the right clinician. This role carries breadth and real ownership from day one with the unique opportunity to work directly with some of the world’s leading AI labs. You will work directly with the Head of Healthcare, Dr Abdul Rahyead (former NHS doctor and ex-founder).

Key responsibilities

  • Research: Staying up to date with academic literature, designing benchmarks and publishing research, building relationships with researchers and industry partners

  • Community Building: Growing the healthcare expert network, handling onboarding, maintaining timely communications and payouts for experts. Exploring creative ways to engage more clinicians through hackathons, platforms and IRL events

  • Business Development: Support commercial and partnership activities, including setting up GTM motions and outreach initiatives

Essential requirements

  • Qualified medical doctor with a minimum of 1 year clinical experience

  • Strong organisation skills with the ability to manage multiple projects at the same time and competing priorities

  • Ability to context-switch between clinicians, customers, projects and operational responsibilities without losing pace or attention to details

  • A proactive, self-directed working style, comfortable operating in an environment where the processes are still being defined and the playbook is being written in real-time

  • Strong research skills, able to critically appraise academic papers and publish benchmarks

Desirable attributes

  • Previously worked in industry or a startup, scale-up or similarly high-paced setting

  • Familiarity with data annotation/labelling, designing and developing evals for AI models

  • Track record of publishing research and working with academic institutions

  • Experience in a client-facing, commercial or business development role

raw.title: Interim Performance Marketing Manager - 3 month contract
raw.description:
About Bike Club

We're customer obsessed. We put the customer at the heart of everything we do - and we're looking for people who feel the same way.

Bike Club is changing the way families access children's bikes. Through our subscription model, we make it easy for families to get the right bike at the right time, while keeping bikes in circulation for longer.

We are a purpose-led, fast-growing business with a strong focus on customer growth, retention and building a more circular approach to children's cycling.

The Role

We need a commercially driven performance marketer for three months to manage and improve customer acquisition across the UK and Germany while we hire a permanent Performance Marketing Manager. You will manage our performance marketing agency and own delivery of our paid acquisition plan, using customer and commercial data to recommend where to invest, test and optimise. We are also open to a fractional role for the right candidate.

What You'll Do

  • Manage our performance marketing agency and other acquisition partners, challenging recommendations where needed.

  • Oversee day-to-day performance and optimisation of paid acquisition across the UK and Germany.

  • Lead the restructure of paid search around parent needs and intent (sizing, outgrown bikes, exchange) rather than subscription terms.

  • Recommend how acquisition budget is allocated across markets, channels and campaigns.

  • Own reporting on CAC, conversion, ROAS, payback and customer value, working with Finance and Data.

  • Set up a simple test-and-learn roadmap across channels, audiences, propositions, creative and landing pages.

raw.description:
Job title: Applied ML Technical Lead, Defence

Location: London; full in-office working as default

Start date: ASAP

Reports to: CEO

Compensation: Salary and Equity options available for discussion

Clearance: Must be eligible to hold UK Security Vetting Clearance SC or above (no prior clearance required)

Application Deadline: 08/11/26 at 23:59 UK Time

___________________________________________________________________________

Help put frontier AI to work in Defence

Cosine is a UK AI lab building models, applications and training infrastructure for mission-critical organisations.

We build coding agents that work across real software systems, specialised Lumen models, AI-native security products and the infrastructure needed to deploy advanced AI in demanding environments. Our customers include some of the world's largest enterprises, including organisations operating behind strict security, regulatory and technical constraints.

We're also training Lumen Sovereign, the first frontier large language model trained in the UK, with the support of the UK Government.

We're now looking for an Applied ML Technical Lead to help develop and deploy advanced AI capabilities for organisations operating in UK Defence and national security.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will work across machine learning development, deployment and customer-facing technical delivery. You may spend part of your time training and evaluating models on complex sensor data, and part of your time working with Defence stakeholders to understand operational needs, shape priorities and guide delivery.

You will not be expected to act as a traditional project manager. Instead, you will own the technical direction and day-to-day progress of applied ML work, coordinating the people and decisions needed to turn promising research into useful operational capability.

___________________________________________________________________________

What you'll do

  • Build ML capabilities for real Defence problems

  • Design, build, train and evaluate machine learning models for challenging applied Defence and national security use cases.

  • Work on problems involving complex sensor data, signal processing, pattern recognition, classification and multimodal intelligence.

  • Develop and improve model architectures, training pipelines, evaluation frameworks and inference systems.

  • Work with real-world and synthetic datasets to improve model accuracy, robustness and generalisation.

  • Translate research prototypes into reliable, deployable capabilities that operate within demanding technical and security constraints.

  • Work closely with Cosine's ML research and engineering teams while taking direct ownership of technical outcomes.

Lead technical delivery from prototype to deployment

  • Own the technical direction and day-to-day progress of applied ML projects.

  • Turn operational objectives into concrete technical goals, experiments, milestones and success measures.

  • Coordinate work across ML researchers, software engineers, infrastructure teams and external stakeholders.

  • Identify technical dependencies, delivery risks and blockers, and help drive them to resolution.

  • Establish clear evaluation criteria and demonstrate progress through measurable improvements and working capabilities.

  • Balance hands-on engineering with the planning and coordination needed to keep complex technical work moving.

Work directly with Defence customers

  • Engage with technical and operational stakeholders across the UK Defence and national security ecosystem.

  • Understand operational challenges and identify where machine learning can make a meaningful difference.

  • Translate customer requirements and constraints into technical objectives, datasets, experiments and delivery plans.

  • Present technical progress, demonstrate working capabilities and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Build trusted relationships with Defence stakeholders and act as a credible technical counterpart.

  • Help customers understand the practical considerations of integrating and deploying ML systems in their existing environments.

Turn research into operational capability

  • Help deploy ML models into real-world environments, including secure, on-premise and resource-constrained systems.

  • Work on model optimisation, inference performance, integration and reliability.

  • Develop robust approaches to evaluation, validation and continuous model improvement.

  • Understand data availability, access requirements, security restrictions and deployment constraints.

  • Establish feedback loops between operational users and Cosine's engineering teams.

  • Ensure that what we build is not only technically impressive, but genuinely useful to the people relying on it.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for

You'll probably have a background in applied machine learning, ML engineering, research engineering or a similarly technical role, along with experience taking ownership of complex technical work.

You should be comfortable:

  • Writing production-quality Python and working with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch.

  • Building, training, fine-tuning and evaluating machine learning models.

  • Working with complex datasets, designing experiments and interpreting model performance.

  • Understanding the trade-offs between model performance, compute requirements, latency and deployment constraints.

  • Working with engineering infrastructure, including Git, containers, Linux and GPU compute.

  • Taking technical ownership of projects with multiple stakeholders, uncertain requirements and evolving priorities.

  • Communicating technical concepts clearly to researchers, engineers, senior stakeholders and operational users.

  • Moving between model development, customer discussions and delivery planning without losing technical depth.

  • Making sound technical judgements, prioritising effectively and finding practical solutions when the path forward is unclear.

  • You don't need to have worked in Defence before. You do need to be excited by the opportunity to apply advanced ML to difficult, consequential real-world problems.

Nice to have

  • Existing UK security clearance, such as SC or DV, or previous experience working in secure Defence environments.

  • Experience with signal processing, time-series data, sensor fusion, representation learning or machine learning applied to complex real-world datasets.

  • Experience with foundation models, multimodal learning or advanced model training and post-training techniques.

  • Experience deploying ML models to edge devices or constrained compute environments.

  • Familiarity with UK Defence procurement, technical assurance or the national security landscape.

  • Experience leading technical workstreams or working as a technical lead on customer-facing ML projects.

___________________________________________________________________________

What success looks like

In your first three months, we would expect you to:

  • Become the technical lead for a major applied Defence ML programme, with responsibility for its day-to-day technical progress.

  • Build strong working relationships with Cosine's ML researchers, engineers and key Defence customer stakeholders.

  • Develop a clear understanding of the existing models, datasets, technical architecture and operational objectives.

  • Establish a focused delivery plan with clear priorities, milestones, ownership and success measures.

  • Make meaningful hands-on contributions to model development, evaluation or deployment.

  • Identify and begin addressing the most important technical and operational blockers.

  • Demonstrate tangible progress to customer stakeholders and build confidence in Cosine's ability to deliver.

  • Longer term, you'll help take advanced ML capabilities from promising prototypes into operational use, while shaping how Cosine builds and delivers applied AI for Defence and other mission-critical organisations.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why this role matters

Some of the most important applications of AI won't be found in consumer products. They'll be in environments where information is incomplete, systems are complex, security matters and the consequences of getting things wrong are significant.

Cosine is working to bring frontier machine learning into those environments.

Doing that requires more than good models. It requires people who can understand an operational problem, build something that works, make good technical decisions, coordinate the work needed to deliver it and stay close to the customer until it creates real value.

You'll have unusual proximity to cutting-edge ML research, senior Defence stakeholders and the operational challenges that will shape the next generation of AI capabilities.

This role will suit someone who is technically strong enough to build, organised enough to lead technical delivery and curious enough to engage directly with the people using the technology.

If you enjoy being close to the research, close to customers and personally accountable for turning ambitious technology into something real, come and work with us.

Come help make frontier AI useful where it matters most.

___________________________________________________________________________


Cosine is an equal opportunity employer.


We value diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and ways of thinking, and we’re committed to creating an inclusive and respectful workplace.

We encourage applications from anyone who meets the role requirements, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of the hiring process, we’re happy to discuss them.

___________________________________________________________________________

Compensation, Benefits & Ways of Working

We’re an in-office team, five days a week, by design. We believe the work we’re doing benefits from being together, collaborating closely, and building shared context.

What you can expect:

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market

  • Equity / share options, so you share in the upside you help create

  • 30 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Work hard in the office, collaborate closely, and switch off properly

  • Dog-friendly office — bring your dog to work

  • Weekly team breakfast & lunch

  • Monthly socials

  • Pension

  • High-quality equipment to do your best work

We care about focus, sustainability, and doing great work — not performative overwork. We value people who show up, contribute thoughtfully, collaborate well with their colleagues, and then go home.

This role won’t suit everyone. But if you’re looking for a fast-moving environment, close collaboration, and a team that takes both the work and work-life balance seriously, it’s a great place to be.

___________________________________________________________________________

Agency & Data Protection Notice

To comply with UK GDPR and our internal data-protection and equal-opportunity obligations, we only accept candidate applications and agency submissions via our Applicant Tracking System (ATS). This ensures appropriate privacy notices, lawful processing, audibility, and consistent retention controls.

Any CVs or candidate details received outside the ATS (including via email, Slack, or direct message) will be treated as unsolicited, will not be considered as part of the recruitment process, and will not give rise to any fee or payment obligation.

raw.description:
Job title: Machine Learning Engineer – Lumen Enterprise Models (SWE-focused LLMs)

Location: London; full in-office working as default

Start date: ASAP

Reports to: CEO

Compensation: Salary and Equity options available for discussion

Application deadline: 08/11/26 at 23:59 UK time

___________________________________________________________________________

Help train the software engineers of the future

Cosine is building autonomous software-engineering systems for organisations where reliability, security and control matter most.

Our Lumen Enterprise models are designed to work across real codebases. They need to understand unfamiliar architectures, make changes across multiple files, use tools, run tests and produce software that engineers can maintain and trust.

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help train and improve these models.

You’ll work across the full training stack, including pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. This is a truly unique role that will provide exposure across all areas of the model training lifecycle. WE’re looking for someone who is just as happy to profile the training loop, identifying performance bottlenecks and memory leaks, as implementing new RL algorithms.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working close to the model and cares about the quality of the software it produces.

___________________________________________________________________________

The role

You’ll work closely with research, infrastructure and product to answer questions such as:

  • What should Lumen learn next?

  • Which data and environments will teach it most effectively?

  • How should we reward correct, maintainable and useful software?

  • How do we train models to work across large repositories and long contexts?

  • How do we know when a model is genuinely better for engineers?

The models you train will write code, use development tools, run tests and receive feedback from real software-engineering environments. Your work will directly influence how Lumen reasons about code, navigates unfamiliar systems and improves through experience.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why this role matters

The best coding models are not simply the ones that generate plausible code.

They need to understand context, respect existing architecture, use tools effectively, test their work and recover when their first attempt fails. They need to produce changes that work in the real world, not just on a benchmark.

That behaviour has to be trained.

You’ll work directly on the data, environments, rewards and evaluations that shape Lumen’s capabilities. Your work will influence the models used by engineers and enterprise teams working on complex and security-sensitive software systems.

This is an opportunity to work on frontier model training while staying close to a concrete, high-value outcome: building AI that can genuinely do software engineering.

___________________________________________________________________________

What you’ll do

  • Work across the full training lifecycle, running pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning experiments.

  • Optimize training methods at scale on frontier models.

  • Diagnose and fix performance bottlenecks and communication overhead in distributed training environments.

  • Train models on long-context, multi-file and repository-level tasks.

  • Develop RL and RLVR loops using signals from execution, tests, linters, static analysis and other engineering feedback, turning fresh ideas into scalable, reproducible code.

  • Investigate model failure modes such as poor planning, brittle fixes, reward hacking and regressions.

  • Collaborate with infrastructure, platform and data teams.

___________________________________________________________________________

Data Enablement Officer
raw.description:
At Efficio, we're not just a consulting firm; we're a team of dedicated experts committed to transforming procurement and supply chain functions. Our mission is to drive sustainable, measurable value for our clients through innovative solutions and deep industry insights. Join us and be part of a dynamic environment where your skills and ideas make a real impact.

Efficio is the world’s largest specialist procurement and supply chain consultancy, with offices across Europe, North America, and the Middle East. We’re a diverse team of over 1,000 individuals, representing more than 60 different nationalities and speaking 40+ languages – and we’re continuing to grow rapidly!

Data Enablement Officer

Help shape how Efficio uses data responsibly, securely and effectively.

We are looking for a Data Enablement Officer to establish and lead Efficio’s data governance framework, helping us protect client data while enabling its responsible use across our services, analytics, products and AI capabilities.

This is a highly visible role at the intersection of data, technology, AI, risk and client delivery. You will work across the business to turn complex contractual, regulatory, privacy and security requirements into practical guidance that enables teams to innovate with confidence.

Initially, the role will have a strong advisory and enablement focus: helping teams understand client requirements, assess new uses of data and make proportionate, risk-based decisions. As our governance model matures, the role is expected to take greater ownership of the framework and delegated authority for lower-risk decisions.

What you'll be doing

Establish our data governance framework

You will assess our current data-handling practices and develop a practical, scalable governance framework covering the lifecycle of client data – from collection and classification through to access, use, sharing, storage, retention and secure deletion.

You will develop and maintain policies and standards covering areas including:

  • Client data handling and classification

  • Data reuse and fair usage

  • Use of client data within Efficio products

  • Use of data with AI tools, including third-party and self-hosted solutions

  • Data access and security

  • Retention, archiving and secure disposal

  • Anonymisation and aggregation

  • Third-party data sharing

  • Policy exceptions and escalation

You will also help establish and maintain our information asset inventories, data flows and AI asset registers.

Enable responsible use of data and AI

A key part of the role will be helping teams determine what we can do with data, under what conditions, and with what safeguards.

You will establish a consistent approach for assessing new and changing data use cases, considering factors such as:

  • Why the data was originally obtained

  • Client and contractual restrictions

  • Data sensitivity and classification

  • The proposed use and intended recipients

  • Security and access controls

  • Retention requirements

  • Legal, client and reputational considerations

For AI use cases, you will help define which activities are permitted, restricted, require additional review or are prohibited. This will include the use of prompts, uploaded files and connected data sources, as well as expectations around human oversight, output validation and accountability.

Govern products, platforms and technology

You will define the conditions under which client data can be stored or processed using Efficio products, SaaS platforms, cloud services and AI tools.

Working closely with Technology, Information Security, Legal and Privacy teams, you will assess areas including:

  • Data residency and international transfers

  • Encryption, access controls and logging

  • Supplier and subcontractor access

  • Data retention, backups and deletion

  • Exit and data-export arrangements

  • Use of customer data for AI model training, product improvement or other secondary purposes

You will help ensure that unapproved platforms are not used for client data without appropriate assessment and documented approval.

Support new solutions and innovation

You will work alongside teams designing and deploying new data, software, analytics and AI solutions, providing governance input from an early stage.

Ahead of launch, you will help confirm that the appropriate governance, legal, privacy and security reviews have taken place and that material risks have been appropriately addressed.

Where issues remain, you will recommend practical remediation, escalation or, where necessary, a delay to rollout. Acceptance of significant residual risk will remain with the appropriate executive or governance committee.

Build governance that works in practice

This role isn't simply about writing policies. We want to create a governance model that teams can understand and use.

You will help develop:

  • A clear data governance operating model and decision-rights framework

  • Practical data, AI, security, reuse and retention policies

  • Data and AI use-case assessment processes

  • Risk-classification and escalation models

  • Policy exception processes and decision registers

  • Product and AI platform assessment standards

  • Solution launch-readiness checklists

  • Training, guidance and supporting materials

  • Governance reporting for senior leadership and relevant committees

You will coordinate, advise and constructively challenge stakeholders across the organisation while recognising that responsibility for managing data risk is shared across business owners, data owners, Legal and Privacy, Information Security, Technology and senior governance forums.

Client engagement

This will also be an important client-facing role.

You will participate in client discussions where required, confidently explaining Efficio's approach to data governance, security and responsible data use.

You should be comfortable responding to questions about how client data is accessed, used, stored, shared, retained and protected, translating technical or governance concepts into clear, credible explanations for different audiences.

What we're looking for

We are looking for someone with experience across one or more of the following areas:

  • Data governance or data management

  • Data privacy

  • Information security

  • Technology or operational risk

  • AI governance or responsible AI

You will also bring a practical understanding of modern technology environments, including SaaS, cloud, analytics and AI platforms.

You'll be someone who can operate comfortably between policy and practice – able to understand complex requirements while recognising the commercial and operational realities of a consulting and technology-enabled business.

In particular, you will be able to:

  • Translate complex regulatory, contractual and security requirements into practical business guidance

  • Apply proportionate, risk-based judgement rather than relying on a purely rules-based approach

  • Influence and challenge senior stakeholders constructively

  • Work effectively across Technology, Security, Legal, Privacy and business teams

  • Balance commercial objectives and innovation with appropriate governance

  • Communicate confidently with clients and senior internal stakeholders

  • Build processes and frameworks that are robust without creating unnecessary bureaucracy

  • Navigate emerging areas where the answer may not always be immediately clear

What success looks like

Success in this role will mean that teams understand how to use data appropriately rather than simply being told what they cannot do.

We will look at measures including adoption of priority policies, review turnaround times, reduction in unapproved tool usage, effective management of exceptions, quality of governance reporting, stakeholder feedback and a reduction in recurring governance issues.

Ultimately, the role will be judged on its ability to achieve both sides of our data ambition: protecting our clients and Efficio while enabling appropriate, secure and innovative use of data and AI.

You will own key client relationships, drive commercial strategy, and oversee multidisciplinary delivery teams to ensure cutting-edge AI deployments are secure, reliable, and grounded in real-world impact.

  • Leading strategic accounts across AI frontier labs, hyperscalers and government entities to build long-term partnerships focused on robust AI safety, evaluation, and red teaming.

  • Designing transformation programmes that integrate advanced AI evaluation methodologies, auditing frameworks, and technical standards directly into mission-critical operations.

  • Partnering with senior client leaders to translate complex safety, governance, and technical AI concepts into actionable strategy and impactful programmes.

  • Overseeing delivery excellence across cross-functional teams of engineers, researchers, and delivery leads to ensure high-stakes projects succeed.

  • Developing commercial strategies and proposals that expand our work across safety-critical domains while meeting ambitious growth goals.

  • Championing thought leadership by sharing insights on AI safety frameworks, emerging risk evaluation, and industry standards with senior stakeholders

 

Who we're looking for:

 

  • You bring deep expertise in AI safety, auditing, ethics, or evaluation methodologies, developed through time in government, research labs, or tech-forward environments.

Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the Team

Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and MedTech start-ups to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.

About the role

Join us as a Lead Machine Learning Engineer to spearhead the technical direction and delivery of complex, innovative AI and software projects. You will act as a technical expert, applying your skills across various projects from solution architecture to client-side deployments, while ensuring engineering decisions are sound and reliable.

This role demands a balance of deep technical expertise and strong leadership, focusing on driving innovation, fostering team growth, and building reusable solutions across the organisation. If you're ready to manage high-risk projects and deliver practical, innovative outcomes, this is your chance to shape our future.

What you'll be doing

  • Setting the technical direction for complex ML and software projects, balancing trade-offs, and guiding team priorities

  • Architecting, implementing, and maintaining reliable, scalable ML/software systems, and justifying key architectural decisions.

  • Defining project problems, developing roadmaps, and overseeing delivery across multiple workstreams in often ill-defined, high-risk environments.

  • Driving the development of shared resources and libraries across the organisation and guiding other engineers in contributing to them.

  • Leading hiring processes, making informed selection decisions, and mentoring multiple individuals to foster team growth.

  • Proactively developing and executing recommendations for adopting new technologies, tools and changing our ways of working to stay ahead of the competition.

  • Acting as a technical expert and coach for customers, accurately estimating large work-streams and defending rationale to stakeholders.

Who we're looking for

  • You are a technical expert among your peers, capable of going deep on particular topics and demonstrating breadth of knowledge to solve almost any problem.

  • You possess strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one compiled or strongly-typed language (e.g. Go, Java, Rust, or TypeScript), and know how to build robust, production-grade systems.

  • You are an expert in at least one major Cloud Solution Provider (e.g., Azure, GCP, AWS) and have led teams to build full-stack web applications.

  • You have hands-on experience with containerisation tools like Docker and orchestration via Kubernetes.

  • You can successfully manage and coach a team of engineers, setting team-wide development goals to improve client delivery.

  • You find novel, clever solutions for project delivery and take ownership for successful project outcomes.

  • You're an excellent communicator who can proactively help customers achieve their goals and guide both technical teams and non-technical stakeholders.

Our Interview Process

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

  2. Introduction to the role (45 minutes)

  3. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes)

  4. System Design Interview (90 minutes)

  5. Commercial & Leadership Interview (60 minutes)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

raw.title: Staff Digital Marketing Manager
raw.description:
What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

 

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

 

Does this sound like you?

You’re a senior digital marketing leader who has owned strategy at scale, you’re as comfortable presenting to executives as you are getting hands-on with performance data. You know how to turn insight into clear commercial decisions and how to build and develop a high-performing team, and you have the credibility to keep digital front and centre in senior conversations. You’re also curious about how AI is changing search, and ready to grow your expertise as it evolves.

 

What you'll do

You'll report to the Head of Digital and CRM and own our digital marketing strategy and implementation from end to end. As the senior strategic voice for digital, you'll turn data and market insight into a clear, commercially led strategy, and make sure every channel and partner delivers to a high standard. You'll also be the link between digital performance and the wider business, keeping digital front and centre in executive decision-making.

This will include:

  • Owning digital marketing strategy and delivery across all channels, including AI and LLM search visibility, so our approach is joined up and commercial wherever Flagstone shows up

  • Managing our agency and external partner relationships, including performance, commercial terms, and governance

  • Shaping what we need from our marketing technology stack as the landscape evolves

  • Using data and digital expertise to plan budgets, set channel strategy, and guide investment, turning performance insight into clear commercial outcomes

  • Giving senior leaders clear, credible, and timely updates on digital performance and strategy

  • Building and developing a high-performing digital team, with the capability, structure, and culture to make digital a key driver of Flagstone's long-term growth strategy

 

What you'll bring

  • Substantial experience in a senior digital marketing leadership role, with hands-on expertise across digital channels and agency management

  • A track record of setting and delivering digital strategy at scale

  • Strong commercial and data skills, with the ability to turn performance data into clear recommendations and sound investment decisions

  • Confidence and credibility when presenting digital performance and strategy to senior leaders and executives

  • Proven people leadership experience, with a track record of managing, developing, and growing high-performing teams

  • Working knowledge of AI and large language model (LLM) search visibility, or the drive to build this expertise quickly as the landscape evolves

  • Experience of thriving in a high-growth, ambitious business, with financial services experience helpful but not essential

     

How we reward you:

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

  • Hybrid working - Spend at least 1 day a week with your team in our collaborative London office

  • Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

  • Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

  • A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

  • Working Abroad - Flagstone employees can work remotely from an approved list of locations for up to 90 days a year

  • Mental wellbeing support – Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill

  • Learning and development – £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.

  • Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

  • Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses

  • Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind

  • Matched pension contributions up to 5%

  • 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

  • Enhanced Parental Leave – enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.

     

All are welcome.

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

raw.title: Developer Portal & Community Manager
raw.description:
We are the creators of Flipper Zero — a portable device for tech enthusiasts and engineers. It’s a gadget with an awesome community that brings together millions of people around the world.

We’re building a new product — Flipper One. It’s a full-featured ARM-based computer running Linux in a compact form factor, powered by the Rockchip RK3576 SoC.

We’ve decided to make the entire development process completely open and public. That’s why we’re looking for a Developer Portal & Community Manager to own and manage the entire Flipper One Developer Portal: maintaining the wiki, collecting tasks from all development teams, managing all GitHub projects and repositories, and proactively communicating with the community.

This role is perfect for you if you want to be close to the product, see firsthand how it’s built, and help turn that process into a clear and valuable entry point for the community. This is not a “content manager” role — you’ll need to fully understand the development process, track all ongoing tasks, and connect the team with the community to make things happen.

What is the Developer Portal?

The Developer Portal is a public wiki + a set of GitHub projects built around Flipper One. It documents how the project works as a whole, explains the architecture of its major subsystems, and provides contribution guides for the community — showing how people can contribute to each sub-project.

Anyone reading the Developer Portal wiki should come away with a complete understanding of the project structure, each feature, and what exactly we are building.

Requirements:

  • You write clearly, concisely, and without fluff, and can show examples of your work: guides, instructions, READMEs, how-tos, or similar materials

  • Basic understanding of hardware, software, and development workflows (Git, commits, branches, pull requests)

  • Able to explain complex technical topics in simple language and visualize them with flowchart sketches

  • Strong verbal communication skills; you know how to listen, ask precise questions, and quickly extract the key points from chaotic discussions

  • Keep communication with the community productive — without toxicity, unnecessary softness, or bureaucracy

  • Comfortable collaborating closely with engineers and navigating technical contexts

  • Discern useful feedback and constructive disagreement from noise and spam

  • Value structure, logic, clarity, and information quality

  • Genuinely interested in developer-facing products, hardware, documentation, open communities, and the build-in-public approach

  • Proficiency in Russian and English for communication with other departments in the company and the external community

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience in DevRel, technical writing, community operations, or an editorial role

  • Experience working with documentation, wikis, knowledge bases, or developer portals

  • Understanding of the culture of technical communities, open-source, and hardware projects

  • Ability to work across topics at the intersection of interfaces, electronics, product architecture, and internal development

Responsibilites:

  • Own and develop the Flipper One Developer Portal

  • Turn the team’s internal context into clear public documentation, notes, updates, and explanations

  • Join team calls to understand what’s actually happening in the project and maintain a complete picture of it

  • Translate technical discussions into clear, human language without losing meaning or accuracy

  • Moderate community comments, pull requests, and contributions

  • Filter out spam, reduce noise, and keep discussions productive

  • Help users understand how the portal works and how to provide useful feedback

  • Collect signals from the community and bring them back to the team

  • Make sure the portal stays structured, up to date, and genuinely useful

What we offer:

  • Fully remote from anywhere in the world

  • You will be provided with all the necessary equipment for a comfortable working environment

  • Benefits such as VHI, corporate sports, foreign language courses, and therapy sessions

  • A five-day workweek with a flexible start of the working day

raw.description:
Metaview is an AI company focused on recruiting. We build AI agents that help world-class companies hire with radically more speed and precision. We automate the toil, and augment the human for companies like Brex, Affirm, Deel, ElevenLabs, and Airtable.

Founded by Siadhal and Shahriar after their experiences scaling Uber and Palantir, we’ve raised $110m from top-tier investors including Google Ventures and Insight Partners.

It's still day 0: Now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with AI at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. We're looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives.

How we work

Four principles guide us:

  • Velocity. Optimize for rate of learning. Take action, get feedback, get better.

  • Hospitality. Sweat the experience. Delight customers, candidates and colleagues, even when it’s inconvenient.

  • Transparency. Public unless private. Share context openly within the company so people and agents can take initiative.

  • End-to-end. Deliver outcomes, not tasks. Step beyond your job description and see the work through.

The role

We're bringing accounting in-house for the first time. Collections, AP, and reconciling across our systems have all been running without a single owner, and that gap is exactly where you'll make your mark early. AI is also rewriting how accounting functions operate, and you'd be building our version of that as we scale, a modern, best-in-class finance function, not a legacy one with AI bolted on. This is a hands-on role reporting directly to the Head of Finance, owning the day-to-day money end to end: collections, AP, payroll, bookkeeping, and month-end close across our US and UK entities.

We're looking for someone a few years post-qualification who has already owned a close and wants to own a whole function next. You'd run it from day one rather than growing into it, and pick up more of our technical accounting, compliance and treasury work as we scale. And we want someone who'd rather build the process than inherit one.

Key ownership areas:

  • Own collections and AP, the single point of contact for customers and vendors.

  • Own month-end close and consolidation across our US and UK entities.

  • Own payroll and sales commissions, working directly with Sales and RevOps.

  • Own the tools behind our finance stack, from selection through implementation, and keep spend under control.

  • Build AI-driven automation into reconciliations, reporting, and close.

What you bring

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent) with a few years in-house since qualifying.

  • You've owned a month-end close end to end, not supported one.

  • Multi-entity or cross-border (US/UK) experience.

  • You take a process and own it - you'd rather deliver finished work than ask permission at every step.

  • You find building the playbook appealing.

  • You double-check everything and usually catch what others miss.

  • You're excited to use AI to make accounting work faster and more accurate, not just to use the tools you're handed.

What we offer

  • The best co-workers you'll ever have, in an environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance.

  • Supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with AI.

About Moneybox
 
At Moneybox, our mission is to give everyone the means to get more out of life. Job Brief

Moneybox serves more than 2M customers and runs a live service handling over 20M API requests a day. We have agreed a company-wide AI Platforms strategy and are building a new AI Deployment team to deliver on it. This is the first of several Senior AI Deployment Engineer hires, reporting to the Head of AI Platforms & Deployment.

You will be a forward-deployed senior engineer who unlocks AI-driven solutions to business problems: an expert in deploying AI and using it safely, not an ML modeller. The work is mainly Python across the modern AI engineering stack - harness engineering, skills and tool building, agent workflows and orchestration, agent hosting and sandboxing, guardrails, evals, RAG and context engineering, and tokenomics (cost, latency, model selection). Production-grade LLM system experience is the core requirement.

You will work on three types of project:

  • Departmental engagements. Embed with departments to AI-enable tasks and processes in a more sophisticated way than "just ask Claude" - for example, Python pipelines where one step is an LLM API call - delivering real incremental value with each engagement and transforming working patterns into load-bearing, AI-enabled business processes.
  • Customer-facing AI deployment. Deploy and integrate AI components built by our ML and Decisioning teams into production: the engineering implementation layer between a working model and a live customer feature.
  • AI platform capabilities. Work with the AI Platforms team to turn engagement patterns into safe, increasingly self-serve company-wide tooling.

Departments across Moneybox are already building AI tools themselves - we want to provide them with a safe path to load-bearing use at scale. This role catches that demand and matures it properly.


What You'll Do
  • Own engagement delivery end to end. Scope with the department, design the solution, build it, deploy it, and agree the handover and ownership model - from prototype through to stable production. Engagements arrive as vague pain; you define the problem, not just the solution.
  • Engineer AI solutions properly. Pipelines, LLM API integration, evals, guardrails, monitoring, and cost and accuracy optimisation for the systems you build. Know when a step must be deterministic and when an LLM is the right tool.
  • Graduate tools into business systems. Take shared, team-load-bearing tools that people have built for themselves and rebuild them as owned business systems under a full SDLC where the value justifies it.
  • Deploy ML-built components into production. Serving, integration with the Moneybox platform, and everything surrounding the model, in partnership with Decisioning and Data Science teams (who own what happens inside the model) and our engineering squads.
  • Build reusable capability. Convert engagement learnings into shared tooling, templates, playbooks and self-serve workflows on the AI Platforms stack. Building out platform components including guardrails, sandboxing, workflows, and gateways.
  • Raise the bar. Work alongside embedded specialists during the team's ramp-up, absorbing and internalising their output so the capability stays with Moneybox.

    • In your first three months we expect your first departmental engagements to be selected on feasibility and delivered with measurable business value - time saved, cost avoided, risk removed - and at least one ML-built capability deployed to production with proper evals, monitoring and cost controls.

    This role is explicitly not ML model training or data science, and it is not a chatbot-prompting generalist: this is production software engineering with AI at its core.


    Who You Are
  • A production engineer with AI at the core. You have built and shipped LLM-powered systems that ran in production and can talk concretely about evals, failure modes, cost curves, and what you would do differently.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity. You can walk into a department with a vague problem and leave with a scoped, deliverable system, and you are managed by exception rather than by direction.
  • A strong partner to non-technical owners. Embedding, scoping and communicating with people who own a business process but not the technology is the job, not a distraction from it.
  • A platform thinker. You have turned one-off solutions into reusable tools or platforms before and you look for the pattern in every engagement.
  • Operationally minded. You care about monitoring, cost and reliability of what you ship, and about making a prototype into a system someone can rely on.
  • Safety-conscious by habit. PII handling, data-boundary discipline, prompt-injection awareness, human-in-the-loop design and graceful failure are how you build, not a checklist you apply afterwards.

    • Skills & Experience

    Essential

  • 5+ years of software engineering with meaningful production ownership.
  • Has built and shipped LLM-powered systems that ran in production.
  • Production-grade Python as your primary language.
  • LLM-powered systems in production: real-world experience working with models via APIs - harnesses, orchestration, structured output, tool use and agents, RAG where appropriate.
  • Evals and quality: designing evaluation sets, measuring accuracy, recall and precision for LLM steps, regression-testing prompts and workflows.
  • Safety and guardrails in practice: PII handling, data-boundary discipline, prompt-injection awareness, human-in-the-loop design.
  • Cost and performance optimisation: model selection, caching, batching, token economics, latency budgets.
  • Deployment and operations: CI/CD, containerisation, monitoring and alerting for AI workloads.
  • Data processing fundamentals: pipelines, transformation, validation, anomaly handling.
  • Customer- or stakeholder-facing delivery experience: consultancy, forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or embedded or platform roles serving non-engineering users.

    • Desirable

  • Experience with Azure and/or .NET. We host on Azure and our core stack is .NET, so willingness to integrate with both is required; existing expertise is a bonus rather than a requirement.
  • Experience with agent hosting and sandboxing platforms, LLM or MCP gateways, or agentic workflow orchestration tooling.
  • Experience in financial services or another regulated environment.
  • Experience deploying models built by a data science team into customer-facing production systems.

Hire, line-manage and set the engagement priorities and delivery standards for a team of forward-deployed AI engineers, working alongside embedded specialists while we hire. raw.title: Performance Engineer
raw.description:
UK | Full-Time

The Mission: Source.dev

Our founders spent over a decade at Google shaping the Android operating systems - building and shipping the software that now runs on billions of devices. They didn't just use Android; they led teams responsible for the Android Virtualization Framework, Security, and the Android Runtime (ART).

Through that journey, they saw a quiet but massive crisis: as device software grew in complexity, the tools used to build it remained stuck in the past. Today, a standard Android checkout exceeds 200GB of code, and builds can take hours. This "wait time" is the single biggest tax on innovation.

Source.dev was founded to reimagine software development workflows for device makers. We’re building a new generation of software tools that make building complex device software feel as simple as building a webpage - starting with SourceFS.

The Core Product: SourceFS

SourceFS is a high-performance virtual filesystem designed to turn multi-hour workflows into minutes.

  • 10x Faster Builds: Intelligent caching and virtualization that only materializes files when they are actually needed.

  • 10x Lower Costs: Enabling a standard 16-vCPU machine to outperform even a 128-vCPU machine.

  • True Engineering Productivity: Replaying hundreds of thousands of build steps instantly when inputs match.

The Cultural Anchor: Own It

We operate with a high degree of trust and a shared value of End-to-End Ownership:

"We own our work end-to-end, from spark to finish. It’s about more than just tasks; it’s the dedication to see things through, staying curious to solve problems, thinking from first principles and ensuring we fix our customer’s problems in the best possible way.”

The Role: Pushing the Speed Limits of Rust, Linux & I/O

We are looking for a Performance / Systems Engineer to join us at Source.dev. In this role, your primary metric of success is speed. You will dissect execution paths, eliminate kernel-space context-switching costs, optimize memory layouts, and ensure SourceFS runs as close to the hardware limits as physically possible.

What You’ll Work On

  • System Bottleneck Hunting: Profile, trace, and eliminate latency across CPU, memory, and disk I/O bottlenecks in Rust systems code using tools like perf, eBPF, valgrind, and custom microbenchmarks.

  • Kernel & File System Tuning: Deep dive into Linux kernel interactions, optimizing FUSE drivers, VFS caches, asynchronous I/O (io_uring), memory-mapped execution, and thread scheduling.

  • Memory & Cache Efficiency: Optimize data structures for cache locality, minimize allocation overhead, and eliminate unnecessary memory copies across boundary transitions.

  • Benchmarking Infrastructure: Design robust, reproducible benchmarking suites to measure micro- and macro-performance regression in high-concurrency environments.

  • Scaling Build Primitives: Squeeze peak performance out of massive build graphs (Android, Yocto, and more) running on high-core hardware configurations.

Ideal Candidate Profile:

  • The Performance Systems Mindset: You have a deep understanding of computer architecture (CPU caches, memory barriers, SIMD, system calls) and proven experience writing hyper-optimized code in Rust or C/C++.(or other). No prior experience with Rust required, just a willingness to learn is all we are looking for.

  • Scale-Obsessed: You have experience with (or a burning desire to fix) large-scale build systems and developer tooling.

  • Impact-Driven: You embody the "Own It" mentality - you see a friction point in the developer journey and you don’t stop until it’s gone.

  • Curious & Collaborative: You enjoy translating real-world customer problems into robust, production-grade solutions.

  • Low Ego, High Impact: Beyond being a brilliant coder, you are a thoughtful and empathetic teammate - someone who leads with kindness

  • Feedback Culture Champion: You embrace feedback and provide it thoughtfully; you see open, honest communication as the foundation of great teamwork.

 

A Note on Our Search

We are looking for the best talent, wherever it may be. If you’re on the fence about whether you’re a perfect fit, please do apply - we value diverse backgrounds and unique problem-solving approaches.

Why Join Source.dev?

  • AI-Native Infrastructure: We merge deep systems expertise with AI to solve the "impossible" - using AI to automate complex merges and conflict resolution for the next generation of devices.

  • Architect the Future: Have a direct, visible impact on the infrastructure used to build the world’s most advanced hardware.

  • Early-Stage Ownership: You’ll have a seat at the table to shape our technical roadmap, product direction, and culture from day one.

  • Tier-One Partnerships: Work side-by-side with world-class customers, from global automotive giants to leading cloud providers.

  • Elite Engineering Culture: Join a high-trust & passionate team of engineers

Machine learning is at the heart of Trainline’s mission to help millions of people make sustainable travel choices every day. Our models and AI agents support customers when journeys go wrong, power search and recommendations across our apps and website, find the best fares through pricing and routing optimisation, personalise the experience with generative AI, and make our digital marketing smarter. Our teams own the full lifecycle from idea to production, and work closely with colleagues across the business to grow the impact of ML and AI at Trainline.

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineering Manager to lead a team of 7 ML engineers and data engineers within our Core Experience pillar, which covers Search, Supply and Commerce. Your team’s work sits at the centre of how customers find, compare and buy their tickets. You’ll be accountable for what your team ships and how it ships it: the quality of the systems, the pace of delivery and the growth of the people building them. You’ll work alongside data scientists, software engineers and product managers. You’ll stay close enough to the technical work to make good calls on architecture, trade-offs and risk. What unites us is curiosity, a love of what we do and a desire to make sustainable travel the easy choice.

In this role, you will... 🚄

  • Lead, coach and grow a team of ML and data engineers. That means setting clear expectations, giving regular feedback, managing performance and building an inclusive team where people do their best work

  • Hire for the team, shaping the roles we need and running a fair, rigorous interview process

  • Own delivery: plan and prioritise with your product partners across Search, Supply and Commerce, unblock the team, and ship ML and AI systems that move measurable customer and business outcomes

  • Set the technical direction for your team’s systems, including architecture, build-versus-buy, and knowing when a simpler approach beats a more sophisticated one

  • Make sure the team builds well across the whole lifecycle: reliable data pipelines, high-quality features, rigorous offline and online evaluation (including A/B testing), reliable deployment, monitoring and ongoing maintenance

  • Lead the team in building production-grade agentic systems, using orchestration harnesses such as LangGraph to design multi-step workflows, tool use and human-in-the-loop controls

  • Make evaluation a first-class engineering discipline for LLM and agent work. That means curated eval sets, LLM-as-judge and human review, tracing, regression testing of prompts and agents, and online monitoring of quality, cost and latency

  • Set the guardrails for responsible use of AI, covering safety, privacy and clear fallbacks when an agent shouldn’t act on its own

  • Raise the bar on engineering practice through code and design reviews, CI/CD, MLOps, observability and on-call

  • Build strong relationships with senior leaders and partner teams, explaining progress, trade-offs and impact in plain language

  • Contribute to our wider AI and ML community and help keep a culture of learning, curiosity and experimentation

We’d love to hear from you if you have... 🔎

  • Experience line-managing engineers, including hiring, performance management and career development

  • A strong background as an ML engineer, with a track record of taking models into production and keeping them healthy at scale

  • Enough grounding in data engineering (pipelines, data modelling and data quality) to lead data engineers as well as ML engineers

  • Solid Python and software engineering fundamentals, with enough hands-on depth to review code and designs credibly

  • Depth in at least one area such as ranking and recommendation, predictive modelling, optimisation or NLP, backed by a solid grasp of statistics, experimentation and feature engineering

  • Experience with modern ML infrastructure on a major cloud platform, ideally AWS, covering distributed data processing, orchestration, model management and infrastructure as code

  • Hands-on experience shipping agentic or LLM-based systems, including agent orchestration frameworks, tool use, RAG, and fine-tuning where it earns its place

  • A disciplined approach to evaluating LLM and agent systems, using tools such as Braintrust, and a clear view on how to know whether an agent is working well in production

  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical colleagues, and good judgement on priorities when there’s more to do than people to do it

Our tech stack 💻

We build mostly in Python on AWS, and choose tools for what they do in production rather than for novelty. You don’t need to know all of it on day one.

  • Data and compute: S3, Athena, Spark on EMR, SQL

  • Orchestration and MLOps: Airflow, MLflow, Docker, ECS, Terraform, GitHub Actions for CI/CD

  • Models: foundation models served through Amazon Bedrock

  • Agents: LangGraph for orchestration, deployed and run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with MCP for tool integration

  • Evaluation: Braintrust for evals, tracing and monitoring agent quality in production

You’ll provide high quality support in relation to both core HR processes and ad-hoc projects and quickly become an integral part of the team and wider business.

If you’re successful in your application, you’ll be joining an enthused and high performing team, one which prides itself on providing stellar service at every stage of the employee life cycle, from on-boarding to off-boarding and everything in between.

As a People Operations Advisor at Trainline, you will...🚅

  • Provide high-quality first-line support to Trainliners and resolving HR process and policy queries professionally and within agreed SLAs.

  • Produce and maintain accurate people data, ensuring high data integrity in our HRIS (HiBob) and that updates are completed promptly. Apply a data-literate, analytical mindset to validate information and produce reports that support People Ops delivery and decision-making.

  • Deliver change alongside day-to-day People services by contributing to People Ops projects such as system enhancements, process redesign, and embedding AI-enabled solutions, while balancing inbox SLAs, operational deadlines, and project work through effective planning and prioritisation to ensure reliable delivery.

  • Work with People Business Partners to support cyclical People processes and document and implement employee lifecycle changes, including personal and contractual updates.

  • Support the preparation, validation, and processing of the monthly UK payroll, ensuring accurate and timely data inputs and alignment between HiBob and payroll workflows.

  • Deliver day-to-day benefits administration, managing enrolments and changes accurately and resolving benefit-related issues efficiently.

  • Manage employee lifecycle administration, including pre-boarding, contracts, background checks, Right to Work documentation, and visa sponsorship, ensuring employee data is accurate across systems and workflows.

  • Process People-related invoices and purchase orders accurately, partnering with accounts payable and supporting effective financial administration.

  • Support and manage the improvement, implementation, and documentation of People policies, processes, and templates, ensuring they remain up to date, user-friendly, and aligned with a tech-first, self-service culture.

Based on the sensitive nature of the role, it’s important that you bring the appropriate degree of discretion and empathy in the way you operate. To this end, you’ll be responsible for identifying escalation points and making sure that any issues are managed appropriately and are dealt with efficiently. Furthermore, being heavily involved in all our HR processes means that you’ll be ideally placed to contribute towards the development of new solutions that further enhance the quality, competence and effectiveness of our current offering.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • You bring a solid foundation in People Operations and are motivated to continue learning and developing in a fast-moving, tech-enabled environment.

  • Working understanding of HR best practices, employment law, and core HR processes, with the ability and curiosity to stay up to date with regulatory change.

  • Experience supporting payroll administration, including maintaining payroll data, running checks, and a working understanding of UK tax, NI, and statutory requirements.

  • Comfortable working with HR systems (ideally HiBob or similar HRIS), with a genuine interest in using technology to improve People processes.

  • Data-literate, with the ability to produce, interpret, and validate reports, ensure data quality, and use insights to support People Partners and business needs

  • Exposure to process and ways-of-working improvement, such as documenting workflows, testing system enhancements, refining templates, or supporting change implementation.

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when handling people data, contracts, payroll inputs, or employee records.

  • Clear and professional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain policies and processes confidently.

  • Strong organisational and time-management skills, able to manage competing priorities, balance BAU and project work, and work to agreed SLAs.

  • Confident using Microsoft Office or Google Workspace, particularly Excel / Sheets for data handling and reporting.

We’re looking for a team player with a ‘roll your sleeves up’ attitude. A self-starter with a helpful, people-orientated demeanour and a high degree of integrity and confidentiality, someone itching expand upon their HR and payroll experience. This is fantastic opportunity for someone who is passionate about HR, keen to work in a fast-moving, forward-thinking technology business, and looking to develop their career.
